    CreatePageBase

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Pages.Common · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/CreatePageBase.cs:21 · Level 3 · class (abstract)

    • What it is: the shared base for an admin create form. It owns the submit pipeline every such page otherwise repeats: validate the form, run an optional pre-check, save with PageToken, clear the dirty flag before the page's own success step, keep a failed Result for the error summary, and always end the saving state (class summary, lines 9-14). The page owns its model and its service call (ADR-146).
    • Depends on: CancellablePageBase (its base and the source of PageToken), IToastService, CreateSubmitOptions, ErrorMessages (ValidationError), ResultUiExtensions (NotifyOnFailure), and Result / Result<T>. External: MudBlazor's MudForm.
    • Concept introduced, the create-form submit pipeline. [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety] assesses that a form validates before it saves, cannot double-submit, keeps the failure visible, and does not leave an unsaved-changes prompt armed after a successful save. [Rubric §18, UI Architecture & Component Design] assesses the reuse. The class remarks (lines 15-20) spell out the page's half of the contract: bind @ref="Form", feed SaveResult to <ErrorSummary>, read IsDirty in the unsaved-changes guard, call MarkDirty from each field's @bind-Value:after, and put the success toast and navigation in the onCreated callback.
    • Walkthrough:
      • Surface (lines 24-39): the injected Toast (line 24, protected), the Form ref (line 27), and three protected properties with private set: IsSaving (line 30), IsDirty (line 33) and SaveResult (line 36). MarkDirty() (line 39) is the one-line setter.
      • SubmitAsync<TCreated>(saveAsync, onCreated, options) (lines 53-110): guards both delegates (lines 58-59) and returns false when Form is unbound or a save is already in flight (line 61), which is the double-submit guard. It defaults options (line 66), clears SaveResult (line 67) and validates (line 68); an invalid form toasts ErrorMessages.ValidationError as a warning and stops (lines 69-73). A non-null PreCheck message toasts as a warning and stops (lines 75-80).
      • The save (lines 82-109): sets IsSaving, awaits saveAsync(PageToken) (line 85), and on success clears SaveResult and IsDirty before calling onCreated (lines 86-92), so the navigation in that callback is not stopped by the unsaved-changes guard. On failure it keeps the result in SaveResult (line 94) and, when ToastOnFailure, calls result.NotifyOnFailure(Toast, options.Localizer) (lines 95-98). An OperationCanceledException returns false (line 102), and the finally always clears IsSaving (lines 106-109). The return value is true only when the save succeeded and onCreated ran.
    • Why it's built this way: the order inside SubmitAsync is the part each page used to get subtly wrong (the dirty flag cleared after navigation, a missing finally, a second click starting a second save). Owning the order in one base means a page supplies only the two things that differ: its service call and its success step.
    • Where it's used: ADC's Conference create pages pass a CreateSubmitOptions to it (for example MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Events/EventCreate.razor.cs, ActivityCreate.razor.cs, SponsorCreate.razor.cs). FormsConventionTestsBase (MMCA.Common/Source/Hosting/MMCA.Common.Testing.Architecture/Bases/Ui/FormsConventionTestsBase.cs) names this base in its form conventions, exercised by MMCA.Common/Tests/Architecture/MMCA.Common.Architecture.Tests/Ui/FormsConventionTestsBaseTests.cs. Behavior is covered by MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Pages/Common/CreatePageBaseTests.cs.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: whether a given ADC create page inherits through @inherits in its .razor or in its code-behind is not visible from the usage scan; ErrorSummary is a Razor component, so what it renders from SaveResult is not verifiable here. An exception other than OperationCanceledException from saveAsync or onCreated propagates to the page after IsSaving is cleared.

    DetailPageBase

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Pages.Common · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DetailPageBase.cs:27 · Level 3 · class (abstract)

    • What it is: the shared framework base for a single-aggregate detail page (loaded by route id, edited inline). It owns the concerns every such page otherwise repeats: a LatestLoadGuard for route-driven reloads, the load outcome (LoadState, set through BeginLoad / CompleteLoad), and the inline edit-mode lifecycle (IsEditing / IsDirty plus the enter and leave transitions the unsaved-changes guard reads). The page-scoped cancellation token and its dispose pattern come from its base, CancellablePageBase (class DetailPageBase : CancellablePageBase, line 27).
    • Depends on: CancellablePageBase (PageToken, Dispose), the sibling LatestLoadGuard it exposes through LoadGuard (line 34), DetailLoadState (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/PageState/DetailLoadState.cs:8, values Loading, Loaded, NotFound, Failed), Result, and ResultUiExtensions.IsNotFound (ResultUiExtensions, MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/ResultUiExtensions.cs:306).
    • Concept: the detail-page counterpart of the list-page base, DataGridListPageBase<TDto>: the same stale-load and dirty-tracking plumbing, but for the one-aggregate-by-id shape instead of the paged-grid shape. The inherited PageToken is handed to every awaited call the page makes outside the guarded load (class remarks, lines 17-20), so navigating away, or an InteractiveAuto render-mode transition swapping the component out, cancels the in-flight work. LoadGuard (line 34) is the companion for the route-driven load itself, and BeginLoad / CompleteLoad wrap it so the page also learns where the load stands: a record that does not exist and a record that could not be fetched never share the same "not found" body (doc comment on LoadState, lines 36-40). [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety] applies to that split and to the dirty flag.
    • Walkthrough:
      • LoadGuard (line 34): a protected LatestLoadGuard property, disposed with the page. Begin() at the start of each load cancels the load it supersedes, and IsCurrent(generation) after each await tells a stale response to leave the page state alone.
      • LoadState (line 41): protected with private set, starting at DetailLoadState.Loading. A page renders DetailLoadStateContent for every state but Loaded.
      • BeginLoad() (lines 48-53): calls LoadGuard.Begin(), puts LoadState back to Loading, and returns the (CancellationToken Token, int Generation) pair the load passes to its awaited calls and completes with.
      • CompleteLoad(generation, result) (lines 67-84): returns false without touching anything when LoadGuard.IsCurrent(generation) is false (a newer load superseded it); otherwise sets LoadState to Loaded and returns true on success, or to NotFound when result.IsNotFound() and Failed for every other failure, returning false. A true return is the page's permission to adopt the value.
      • IsEditing / IsDirty (lines 87, 90): both protected with private set, so only the transition methods below can move them.
      • MarkDirty() (line 93): the one-line setter bound to every editable field's @bind-Value:after.
      • ClearDirty() (line 99): clears the dirty flag without opening or closing the editor, for a child panel that reports its own dirty state in both directions while the page's editor state stays as it is.
      • BeginEdit() (lines 102-106) and EndEdit() (lines 109-113): open the editor on a clean slate, and close it clearing the dirty flag, so the dirty flag can never be left set behind a closed editor.
      • Dispose(bool) (lines 120-129): protected override; when disposing it disposes LoadGuard (idempotent, so a second dispose stays a no-op) and then calls base.Dispose(disposing), which cancels and disposes the page-scoped source once. Putting the load outcome next to the load guard means the not-found versus failed decision is made once, from the Result's error type, instead of each page collapsing both into one empty body. The cancellation source moved down into CancellablePageBase so this base and CreatePageBase share one copy of it (ADR-146). Adding a new detail page costs an @inherits line and a BeginLoad / CompleteLoad pair.

LifetimeTokenConventionTests (MMCA.Common/Tests/Architecture/MMCA.Common.Architecture.Tests/Ui/ComponentConventions/LifetimeTokenConventionTests.cs) also names this base.

Whether a given page inherits this base through an @inherits directive in .razor markup rather than in its code-behind is not verifiable from a .cs-scoped scan.

    ListPageActions

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Pages.Common · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/ListPageActions.cs:14 · Level 3 · class (static)

    • What it is: one static helper every admin list page shares: the confirm-delete-toast-reload flow, DeleteWithConfirmationAsync (line 32).
    • Depends on: IToastService, Result, and the DeleteConfirmation dialog component (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Forms/DeleteConfirmation.razor:27).
    • Concept introduced, the shared page helper that stays out of the base class. [Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality] assesses whether a repeated flow exists once; [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety] assesses that destructive actions confirm first and that failures surface to the user. The placement argument is in the class comment (lines 7-13): the flow is a plain static rather than a member on DataGridListPageBase<TDto>, so a page that composes its own layout can reuse it without inheriting anything. The same comment records why the layout reload is not here: it lives on the base as ReloadActiveLayoutAsync (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DataGridListPageBase.cs:1746), because on a phone it must save the page's filters, which only the page can read.
    • Walkthrough: DeleteWithConfirmationAsync(deleteConfirm, entityName, deleteAsync, toast, successMessage, errorMessage, reloadAsync) (lines 32-69) takes the page's DeleteConfirmation ref, the entity display name, a Func<Task<Result>> delete call, the toast service, a localized success message, a Func<Result, string> error mapper, and a reload callback. It guards every reference argument with ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull (lines 41-45), shows the dialog, and returns immediately unless the answer is exactly true (lines 47-51): a dialog dismissed with null is a cancel, not a confirm. On confirm it awaits the delete and branches on the Result (lines 55-60): a failure toasts the mapped error and returns without reloading, a success toasts and awaits reloadAsync (lines 62-63). The single catch (OperationCanceledException) (lines 65-68) is swallowed with a comment naming the two causes, component disposal and the InteractiveAuto render-mode transition.
    • Why it's built this way: passing the localized strings and the error mapper in as parameters keeps this class free of any resource dependency, so each page supplies its own translated text (ADR-027) while the flow itself stays identical everywhere. The errorMessage delegate is what lets a page choose between a fixed sentence and the API's own wording via result.LocalizedErrorMessage(L), which the parameter doc (lines 26-30) spells out. Taking the reload as a delegate is what lets the phone-aware reload stay on the base.
    • Where it's used: Common's own UserAdminList (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Administration/UserAdminList.razor.cs) and ADC's Conference list pages ActivityList, ConferenceCategoryList, EventList, PartnerList, QuestionList, RoomList, SessionList, SpeakerList and SponsorList (under MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/). Covered by MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Pages/Common/ListPageActionsTests.cs.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: DeleteWithConfirmationAsync catches only OperationCanceledException; any other throw from the caller's deleteAsync or reloadAsync delegate propagates to the page's own handler, which is not visible from this file. Store call sites were not part of this unit's usage scan.

    DataGridListPageBase<TDto>

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Pages.Common · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DataGridListPageBase.ColumnFilters.cs:20 · Level 4 · class (abstract, partial)

    • What it is: the abstract Blazor base for every server-paged MudDataGrid<TDto> list page. It folds the otherwise copy-pasted concerns (cancellation lifecycle, loading, failure and confirmed-empty flags, mobile/desktop viewport detection, filter, column-filter and sort extraction and restore, error reporting, scroll tracking and restore, density toggle, URL plus session plus prerender state plumbing, an opt-in virtualization funnel, newest-load-wins ordering for overlapping loads, and disposal) into one reusable component. It is split over two files: the main declaration public abstract partial class DataGridListPageBase<TDto> : ComponentBase, IBrowserViewportObserver, IAsyncDisposable, IDisposable (DataGridListPageBase.cs:24) and the column-filter persistence part (DataGridListPageBase.ColumnFilters.cs:20).
    • Depends on: IToastService, SharedResource (as IStringLocalizer<SharedResource>), ListPageState and its ColumnFilterState entries, ListPageStateService, ListPageQueryStateService, BreakpointConstants, ErrorMessages, ResultUiExtensions (NotifyOnFailure), ComponentLifetimeExtensions (LifetimeToken), MobileInfiniteScrollList<TItem>, QueryFilterKeys (Alias, SearchTag), Result, and the nested PersistedGridState. Externals: MudBlazor's MudDataGrid<T>, GridState<T>, GridStateVirtualize<T>, GridData<T>, FilterDefinition<T>, IBrowserViewportObserver / IBrowserViewportService, and Blazor's PersistentComponentState, NavigationManager, IJSRuntime, RendererInfo.
    • Concept introduced, a behavior-rich Blazor base component. [Rubric §18, UI Architecture & Component Design] assesses reuse, and every list page in both apps inherits this behavior with no copy-paste (ADR-146). [Rubric §23, Front-End Performance & Rendering] assesses render and fetch cost: only the requested page is ever fetched, the prerender cache skips a redundant round trip, and the opt-in virtualization funnel keeps the DOM small for large sets. [Rubric §19, State Management & Data Flow] covers the four-channel persistence (URL, in-memory, sessionStorage, prerender cache), which now carries the grid's own column filters and restored sort as well as the page's filters, and the newest-load-wins rule for overlapping fetches. [Rubric §27, Internationalization] applies because the cancellation toast and every Result failure message resolve through SharedResource. [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety] shows up in two flags: LoadFailed (line 55), because a failed fetch renders zero rows, which is visually identical to a genuinely empty list once the error toast expires, and EmptyConfirmed (lines 66-68), true only when the NEWEST load completed with TotalItems == 0, because the loading state ends and renders before MudDataGrid has received the rows. Many of the members below carry an inline diagnosis of the E2E-discovered defect they fix, touching [Rubric §28, Front-End Testing].
    • Walkthrough, in teaching order (lines are in DataGridListPageBase.cs unless the column-filter file is named):
      • Abstract and virtual surface: derived pages supply the abstract Title (line 72) and may override SaveFilters / RestoreFilters (lines 164, 167), GridRef (line 177), MobileListRef (line 187, the page's card list), OnRestoredStateAppliedAsync (line 622), OnBeforeFetchAsync (line 944), OnMobileDataRequestedAsync (line 1839), and the three virtualization knobs VirtualizeGrid (line 200, default false), VirtualizedGridHeight (line 208, default 70vh) and VirtualizedItemSize (line 216, default 52).
      • Public and protected state: IsLoading (lines 42-44), LoadFailed (line 55), EmptyConfirmed (lines 66-68), IsMobile (line 75), the mobile card-view block MobileItems / MobileTotalItems / MobileCurrentPage / MobilePageSize (lines 78-81), the bindable CurrentPageState (line 88, 0-indexed), RowsPerPageState (line 98, defaulting to 10 to match MudDataGrid v9's own default), and DenseGrid (line 107). IsLoading is computed as field || !RendererInfo.IsInteractive (line 44): always true during the non-interactive SSR prerender pass, because the grid fetches from OnAfterRenderAsync, which a static render never reaches. EmptyConfirmed is its mirror image, field && RendererInfo.IsInteractive (line 68).
      • Constants (lines 113, 117): PrerenderFetchTimeoutMs = 5000 bounds the SSR fetch, and VirtualizedScrollContainerSelector = ".mud-table-container" records where a virtualized grid actually scrolls.
      • Private fields (lines 119-155): the nullable CTS, the _disposed guard, the scroll module and its DotNetObjectReference, the persistence subscription, the prerender caches, _newestPagedLoad (line 127), the saved-state mirrors, _restoredPagePending (line 138), _restoredSortPending (line 145, so a restored sort wins over the default column sort every page seeds), _shadowedGridSort (line 148), _restoreGridAfterWidening (line 151), the re-entrancy and deferral flags, and a per-instance _scrollTrackerId (line 155). The observer contract's Id and ResizeOptions (a 250 ms report rate) sit at lines 158 and 161.
      • OnInitialized (from line 225), synchronously: restores any PersistedGridState under the key grid:{GetType().FullName} (lines 231-232); registers the persisting callback with an explicit RenderMode.InteractiveAuto (line 257); pins _ownRoutePath to this page's route (line 264); reads the URL through ListPageQueryStateService, falling back to the in-memory ListPageStateService snapshot; primes the pager, sort, density and page filters, and takes the restored column filters (RestoreColumnFilters, line 290) so the grid's first ServerData call already fetches the right rows.
      • OnLocationChanged (from line 312): reacts only to same-path back/forward navigation (an Ordinal path compare, line 323), re-reads the URL (including column filters, line 346), and hands off to ReloadActiveLayoutAfterNavigationAsync (line 367): on a phone with a card list it reloads the way a filter change does, through ReloadActiveLayoutAsync; otherwise the grid takes the URL's page, column filters (line 385) and sort and reloads. IsEchoOfSavedState (line 1815) recognizes a location that carries exactly the query the last save wrote. ApplyCurrentPageFromUrl (line 401) is BL0005-suppressed (line 400).
      • Viewport (NotifyBrowserViewportChangeAsync, line 410): recomputes IsMobile from BreakpointConstants. When the viewport widens from the card list back to the grid, PrepareGridRestoreAfterWidening (line 435) seeds the newly created grid from the saved pager and sort, because the new grid starts on page 1 at the default page size and sort.
      • First render: OnAfterRenderAsync (line 462) awaits RunFirstRenderSetupAsync (line 497), which hydrates session state, checks _disposed after each interop round trip, starts scroll tracking (StartScrollTrackingAsync, line 555, importing ./_content/MMCA.Common.UI/list-page-scroll.js at line 568), restores the grid state and awaits OnRestoredStateAppliedAsync. ReleaseLateFirstRenderSetupAsync (line 630) and ReleaseScrollTrackingAsync (line 646) release what the setup created when the page went away mid-setup; JS calls back into [JSInvokable] OnScrollPositionChanged (line 687).
      • Pager and sort restore: RestoreCurrentPageAfterRowsPerPageReset (line 711, BL0005-suppressed at line 710) works around the MudDataGrid v9 RowsPerPage setter that resets CurrentPage. ApplyRestoredState (line 749) feeds the column filters too (line 762). RestoreGridStateAsync (line 772) is the single entry point for the pager-restore machinery, then ApplyRestoredSortOrReloadAsync (line 822) puts the restored column filters on the grid (line 831) and the restored sort through RestoreSort (line 841) and ApplyRestoredSortToGridAsync (line 856). The latter's summary gives the reason: every list page seeds a default column sort, so without it a shared ?s=Name&sd=desc link was rewritten to the default on first load.
      • Column-filter persistence (DataGridListPageBase.ColumnFilters.cs): the grid's own column filters are saved with the rest of the list state (URL c: keys, in-memory state and sessionStorage) and put back on the grid on restore, so a filter survives opening a row and pressing Back, a refresh and a shared link (content comment, lines 7-12). RestoreColumnFilters (line 29) takes the restored set and marks it pending; ResolveColumnFilters (line 49) is what a fetch sends and saves: while a restore is pending (or was pending when the fetch started, the restorePendingAtLoadStart parameter) it builds the restored definitions against the rendered grid, otherwise it uses the grid's own. ApplyRestoredColumnFiltersToGrid (line 75) replaces the grid's FilterDefinitions directly rather than through AddFilterAsync, so the filter panel stays closed and no load starts. SnapshotColumnFilters (line 92) writes values in the invariant culture through FormatFilterValue, and BuildColumnFilterDefinitions drops a saved filter whose column the grid does not render or allow filtering on, or whose value no longer parses (TryParseFilterValue and TryParseDateOrNumber: string, bool, enum, Guid, DateOnly, DateTime round-trip, then numbers through Convert.ChangeType).
      • Paged loads: LoadServerDataAsync (lines 918-929) starts LoadPagedAsync (line 1004), records it in _newestPagedLoad before anything yields, and returns NewestPagedResultAsync (line 1054), so overlapping calls end on the NEWEST call's rows, never a superseded call's empty cancelled page (MudDataGrid applies whichever ServerData call completes last). FetchPagedAsync (line 1071) holds the fetch, awaiting OnBeforeFetchAsync and sending the resolved column filters; FetchWithinRangeAsync (line 1132) fetches the last page instead when the requested page lies past the end, and MovePagerToRows / MovePagerTo (lines 1174, 1188) put the pager on the page the returned rows belong to.
      • OnBeforeFetchAsync (line 944): a protected virtual hook awaited by every loader and by every delegate MobilePageFetcher builds, before the filter bag is built, so a page that must wait for state its filter callback reads (a picker's options loading) waits in one place. The default does nothing; a throw inside a grid loader is reported like a throwing fetch.
      • MobilePageFetcher (line 968): turns the grid's fetch delegate and filter callback into the FetchPageResult delegate a MobileInfiniteScrollList<TItem> takes, so one fetch method serves the grid and the phone list. It applies an optional default sort and an optional afterFetchAsync step, and returns the Result unchanged (no toast, no page state change), because the list owns retry and error display.
      • Virtualized and mobile loads: LoadVirtualizedServerDataAsync (line 1223) maps the row window MudBlazor asks for onto the same page-based fetch through ComputeVirtualWindow (line 1405, internal static so the tests drive it directly). LoadMobileDataAsync (line 1444) is the card-list equivalent, with ClearMobileItems (line 1495) as its page-1 failure shape.
      • One fetch pipeline: RunFetchAsync<TResult> (line 1320) sits behind the paged, virtualized and mobile loaders. It takes the load's own source rather than re-reading _cts, sets and clears the loading and failure flags, runs the caller's fetch inside the try so a throw from page code cannot strand IsLoading, and toasts the localized Grid.Snackbar.LoadCancelled (line 1348) only for a current, undisposed load. FailedFetch<TResult> (line 1383) is the Result-branch counterpart, and EmptyGridData (line 1390) the empty shape. CreateFetchCts (line 1427) links the load's lifetime token, the caller's token, and the 5 s prerender timeout during non-interactive rendering.
      • Load identity: ResetCancellationTokenAsync (line 1506) swaps in a fresh CTS first and returns the source it swapped in. IsCurrentLoad (line 1540) is ReferenceEquals(loadSource, _cts), and ThrowIfSuperseded (line 1547) ends a superseded load on the silent cancellation path.
      • Filters and sort: ExtractGridFilters (line 1566) flattens the grid's filter definitions one entry per column through EffectiveColumnFilters (line 1582); ApplyAdditionalFilters (line 1600) runs the page's callback without letting it overwrite a grid key, moving a clashing value to QueryFilterKeys.Alias(key, QueryFilterKeys.SearchTag). ExtractSortParameters (line 1624) and ResolveSortParameters (line 1637) pick the sort, letting a pending restored sort win over the grid's seeded default.
      • Saving state: SaveCurrentState (line 1689) now also takes the column filters to save, falling back to the stored entry's and then the restored set. SaveFilterState (line 1736) saves the page's filters keeping pager and sort, and ReloadActiveLayoutAsync(mobileList) (lines 1746-1755) reloads whichever layout is rendered: on a phone it saves the filters first and resets the card list from page 1 (the list's fetch saves nothing, so a filter changed there was otherwise lost on leaving); otherwise it reloads GridRef. ToggleDensity / PersistDensity (lines 1762, 1783) and ResolvePagerState (line 1774) complete the persistence.
      • Route pinning and teardown: _ownRoutePath (line 1806), GetRoutePath() (line 1808) and IsOwnRouteCurrent() (line 1832, OrdinalIgnoreCase at line 1833) drop a stale write after navigation. CancelLoading (line 1841) is the manual cancel hook. DisposeAsync (line 1844), Dispose(bool) (line 1872), UnsubscribeLocationChanged (line 1888) and Dispose (line 1897) release the subscription, the scroll module and the CTS, _disposed-idempotent. PersistedGridState closes the file at line 1907.
    • Why it's built this way: every concern here was independently re-implemented (and re-broken) on individual pages before being lifted into one base, so a single fix now propagates to every list page at once. The four-channel persistence covers how a user can leave and return to a list (browser back, in-app navigation, refresh or forceLoad, a shared link), and the column filters and restored sort now travel the same way, so none of those paths silently drops part of what the user set. The delegate signature mirrors IEntityService<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>.GetPagedAsync exactly (remarks at lines 908-916), so a page passes a method group with no adapter. The column-filter logic lives in its own partial file to keep the main file's concerns readable. The phone reload moved here from ListPageActions because it must save the page's filters, which a static helper cannot read.
    • Where it's used: base class for the list pages in both apps, including ADC's PublicSessionListView and PublicSessionList (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Public/Sessions/), ADC's EventFilteredListPageBase (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Common/EventFilteredListPageBase.cs), and Engagement's AttendeeSearchPanel (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/AttendeeSearchPanel.razor.cs); Common's ListPageShell and InfiniteScrollSentinel (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Lists/) reference it. Covered by bUnit tests at MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Pages/Common/DataGridListPageBaseTests.cs and, beside it, DataGridListPageBaseLifecycleTests.cs, DataGridListPageBaseFilterStateTests.cs and DataGridListPageBaseMobileFetchTests.cs, plus the conformance probe Conformance/ProbeListPage.cs.

The prerender optimization assumes a warm backend; under a cold one the prerender fetch times out at 5 s and the interactive pass refills the grid. The list-page-scroll.js module and ListNoRecordsContent are referenced here only by name, so their behavior is not verifiable from these .cs files. The route comparison is Ordinal in OnLocationChanged (line 323) but OrdinalIgnoreCase in IsOwnRouteCurrent (line 1833); the source does not state why the two differ.

    • Concept introduced, enrollment ends the session. [Rubric §11, Security] assesses session and second-factor handling. The class remarks (lines 22-37) state the three rules: the API does not re-issue tokens when enrollment is confirmed and the current token carries no second factor, so once the codes are saved the page signs out and sends the user to sign in again with a password and a code; an account that signs in only through an external provider or a sign-in link sets a password or registers a passkey before enrolling; and the secret and recovery codes live only in this component's memory, never logged, never in the URL, never cached on the device. [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety] applies to the destructive confirm on disable and the single busy flag.
    • Walkthrough:
      • State (lines 40-56): LoginRoute = "/login" (line 40), a page-scoped _cts (line 42), the breadcrumbs, the _state (line 45), the loaded status and its Result, the transient _setup and _codes, _codesFromEnrollment, the action code and error, _recentSignInRequired, _hasMultiFactor, _isBusy and _disposed.
      • Inputs: Required (lines 84-85, [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = "required")]), set when the API refused the session for want of a second factor so the page says the role requires one; the cascading AuthState (line 87); six injected services (lines 89-99).
      • Dispose (lines 102-120): Dispose() delegates to a protected virtual Dispose(bool) that cancels and disposes _cts once.
      • OnInitializedAsync (lines 123-138): builds the localized breadcrumbs (in the method, not a field initializer, so the injected localizer is available), reads HasMultiFactor() from the user (line 134), then LoadStatusAsync (line 140), which sets Enabled or NotEnrolled from the status, or LoadFailed.
      • Enrollment: BeginAsync (line 165) calls BeginEnrollmentAsync and moves to Enrolling. The panel's callbacks land in OnEnrollmentConfirmed (line 194, dropping the secret before the codes are shown), OnEnrollmentCancelled (line 203) and OnRecentSignInRequired (line 209). OnCodesSavedAsync (line 220) then either signs out and back in after an enrollment, with LoginRefusals.TwoFactorEnabledReason, or re-reads the status after a regeneration.
      • Code-proved actions: RegenerateAsync (line 232) and DisableAsync (line 263) both take the trimmed code from ActionCode() (line 340) and claim the busy flag through TryStartAction() (line 325). Disable first asks a destructive confirm through IAppDialogService.ConfirmAsync (lines 272-277). A refusal goes through ShowRefusal (line 354): a recent-sign-in refusal shows the sign-in-again notice, any other shows LoginRefusals.Describe(...).
      • Sign out and back in: SignInAgainAsync (line 305) and SignOutAndSignInAgainAsync (lines 309-321) call LogoutAsync, build /login?reason=..., append a returnUrl only when ReturnUrlProtector.Sanitize (line 314) yields something other than /, and navigate with forceLoad: true (line 320).
    • Why it's built this way: a single state enum plus one busy flag keeps every action mutually exclusive and every transition visible in one file, while the two panels own their own rendering and focus. Signing out after enrollment is the honest answer to a token that cannot gain a second factor in place, and the forced reload ensures no in-memory state from the old session survives.
    • Where it's used: routed through TwoFactorPageGate (TwoFactorPageGate, MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/TwoFactor/TwoFactorPageGate.cs). Covered by MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Pages/Auth/TwoFactor/TwoFactorAccountTestsBase.cs and TwoFactorAccountEnabledTests.cs, and by TwoFactorPageGateTests.cs, TwoFactorRoutesTests.cs and TwoFactorPageAuthorizationTests.cs under MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/TwoFactor/.

Its meaning comes from its co-located resources, whose keys mirror MudBlazor's own LanguageResource keys (v9.6.0) with the English values copied verbatim so en-US behavior is unchanged, and from ResxMudLocalizer, which injects IStringLocalizer<MudTranslations> and hands those strings to MudBlazor's localization interceptor.
    • Concept reinforced, the resource-anchor type. The idiom is introduced in full at SharedResource: ASP.NET Core's IStringLocalizer<T> resolves keys against the .resx whose base name matches T, so a dedicated empty class becomes the name of a shared string table. MudTranslations is the second anchor, scoped to third-party chrome rather than app chrome. [Rubric §27, Internationalization] assesses whether all user-visible copy follows the active culture, including the component library's; [Rubric §20, Design System & Theming] assesses a coherent design system, and a pager that still reads "Rows per page" under an es UI would break that coherence at exactly the surface the user interacts with most.
    • Walkthrough: there are no members. The whole contract is "be a public sealed type named MudTranslations in this namespace, with sibling .resx files whose keys match MudBlazor's LanguageResource". The doc comment (lines 3-9) records the verbatim-English-mirror invariant.
    • Why it's built this way: MudBlazor exposes exactly one extension point for translating its built-in strings (an injectable MudLocalizer), and it needs some resource base to read from. A separate anchor keeps the library's keys in their own table, mirroring the upstream names one to one, cleanly apart from the app's own SharedResource chrome. This is the ADR-027 way to translate a dependency you do not own.
    • Where it's used: injected as IStringLocalizer<MudTranslations> by ResxMudLocalizer, which AddUIShared registers as MudBlazor's MudLocalizer via TryAddTransient (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:129). Because resolution flows through the DI IStringLocalizerFactory, the PseudoStringLocalizerFactory decorator registered at DependencyInjection.cs:123 reaches these strings too.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the .resx files and their per-key match to MudBlazor v9.6.0's LanguageResource are resources, not .cs; individual key contents are not enumerated here.

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Pages.Notifications · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Notifications/NotificationList.razor.cs:114 · Level 0 · record (private, sealed, nested in NotificationList)

    • What it is: one already-localized line of the "Phone" column on the push-notification history page: the text of a per-platform native delivery outcome plus the MudBlazor chip color and icon that go with it. It is declared as private sealed record PhoneDeliveryLine(string Text, Color Color, string Icon); (line 114), so nothing outside NotificationList can see it.
    • Depends on: nothing first-party in its shape. Externals: MudBlazor (Color, and the Icons.Material.Filled string constants its producers pass in).
    • Concept reinforced, the text carries the meaning. The doc comment on the record (line 113) states the rule: the text carries the status, so color and icon are never the only cue. [Rubric §21, Accessibility] assesses whether information survives without color (WCAG 1.4.1, use of color); here a green check, an amber warning and a red error each come with a sentence such as "Android: delivered (1 of 1 batch)", so a screen-reader user or a color-blind operator reads the same outcome. The markup comment repeats the rule where the chip is rendered (NotificationList.razor:96-98).
    • Walkthrough: a positional record with three members. Text is the finished sentence, built by AddPhoneDeliveryLine from the localized Notif.Phone.Line or Notif.Phone.LineNoUnit format (NotificationList.razor.cs:95-97) or, for an unattributed failure, from Notif.Phone.StatusOnly (line 74). Color and Icon come from PhoneDeliveryStatus (lines 101-111): Success with CheckCircle when every attempted unit was delivered, Warning with Warning when some were, Error with Error when none were.
    • Why it's built this way: a private record keeps the three values that must travel together in one immutable value, without adding a public type to the package surface for what is purely a rendering detail of one page.
    • Where it's used: produced only by NotificationList.PhoneDeliveryLines and AddPhoneDeliveryLine (NotificationList.razor.cs:67-99) and consumed only by the Phone cell of the history table, which renders one outlined MudChip per line, or - when the list is empty (NotificationList.razor:99-112).

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Resources · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Resources/SharedResource.cs:9 · Level 0 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: an empty marker class that anchors IStringLocalizer<SharedResource> over its co-located .resx files, the single home for cross-cutting UI chrome strings (ADR-027).
    • Depends on: nothing first-party. The type is empty: public sealed class SharedResource; (line 9). Its meaning comes from the co-located resources SharedResource.resx (the English default) and SharedResource.es.resx (Spanish), named in the doc comment (line 7), and from the ASP.NET Core localization stack that binds IStringLocalizer<T> to the .resx named after T.
    • Concept introduced, the resource-anchor type. [Rubric §27, Internationalization] assesses whether user-facing copy is externalized to per-culture resources keyed stably rather than hard-coded. ASP.NET Core's IStringLocalizer<T> convention resolves keys against the resource file whose base name matches the type T, so a dedicated empty class becomes the name that ties many components to one shared string table: injecting IStringLocalizer<SharedResource> anywhere reads the same dotted, stable keys (Common.Error.Load, Grid.Snackbar.LoadCancelled, Auth.Sessions.Title). The doc comment (lines 3-8) enumerates the chrome it covers: buttons, layout labels, snackbar and error templates, and the culture- and theme-switcher text. Its counterpart for library chrome is MudTranslations.
    • Walkthrough: there are no members. The whole contract is "be a public sealed type named SharedResource in this namespace, with sibling .resx files". The work lives in the key/value pairs and in the localization middleware that resolves them by culture.
    • Why it's built this way: a marker type is the idiomatic ASP.NET Core way to scope a shared resource table without inventing a real class, and one anchor keeps the chrome strings in a single table every component shares (ADR-027).
    • Where it's used: injected as IStringLocalizer<SharedResource> by DataGridListPageBase<TDto> for its cancellation toast and its Result error rendering (DataGridListPageBase.cs:27), by Sessions for every label on the devices page (Sessions.razor.cs:34), by the auth pages for their field labels and messages, and handed to ErrorMessages.Configure from the root layout (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Layout/MainLayout.razor:103) so the static helper resolves the same table.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the .resx files are resources, not .cs; their per-key contents are not enumerated here.

A DataAnnotations attribute on a model property needs its message at attribute-evaluation time, where there is no DI container to inject a localizer from, so the messages are static properties read through a ResourceManager on demand. Each property is a one-line Get("Auth.Field.<Field>.<Rule>") call (lines 24-42): FirstNameRequired, LastNameRequired, EmailRequired, EmailInvalid, PasswordRequired, PasswordMaxLength, PasswordComplexity, ConfirmPasswordRequired, ConfirmPasswordMismatch and TokenRequired. How the model attributes bind to these properties (for example through ErrorMessageResourceType) is in the model files, not in this type.

    NotificationInbox

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Pages.Notifications · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Notifications/NotificationInbox.razor.cs:28 · Level 4 · class (partial, page)

    • What it is: the code-behind for the per-user notification inbox, routed at both @page "/notifications/inbox" and @page "/notifications/inbox/{Id:int}" (NotificationInbox.razor:1-2). It fetches the signed-in user's notifications a page at a time, renders each as a read or unread card, lets the user mark items read individually or all at once, highlights and scrolls to a deep-linked notification, and reloads the current page when a real-time push asks for a refresh. A failed load is also rendered inline: an ErrorSummary bound to the last outcome, plus a Retry button when the list is empty (NotificationInbox.razor:17,40-47).
    • Depends on: first-party: INotificationInboxUIService (the typed read-side HTTP service), NotificationState (the per-circuit unread-count store and refresh signal), UserNotificationDTO (the row shape), IToastService (the toast abstraction), ResultUiExtensions (the NotifyOnFailure helper), SharedResource (the resx anchor for the localizer), ViewerTimeZone (the viewer's clock for sent times, resolved after first render), and ComponentLifetimeExtensions (the LifetimeToken read). Externals: MudBlazor (IScrollManager, ScrollBehavior, BreadcrumbItem, Icons), Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components ([Inject], [Parameter], OnInitializedAsync, OnParametersSet, OnAfterRenderAsync, InvokeAsync, StateHasChanged), Microsoft.Extensions.Localization (IStringLocalizer<T>), BCL CancellationTokenSource, IDisposable, Math.Ceiling, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture.
    • Concept introduced, the Blazor code-behind page pattern (.razor plus .razor.cs partial class). The three notification pages in this unit are authored as partial classes split across two files: the .razor holds declarative MudBlazor markup and the routes, the .razor.cs holds the C# (public partial class NotificationInbox, line 28), the injected services, the view state, and the handlers. The framework constructs the component, calls OnInitializedAsync (line 79, which returns the load task directly rather than being async) once, and re-renders when a handler mutates a field. Four habits recur across all three pages and are worth learning once here:
      • Disposal-safe async with a per-component CancellationTokenSource. A readonly CancellationTokenSource _cts (line 48) is created with the component and its token is read through _cts.LifetimeToken() (ComponentLifetimeExtensions) and passed to every service call (lines 115, 227, 291, 306, 327). Reading .Token off a disposed source throws ObjectDisposedException, so LifetimeToken returns an already-cancelled token instead and the work stops through the normal OperationCanceledException path (ComponentLifetimeExtensions.cs:3-10,26-31). Dispose(bool) (lines 358-370) cancels and disposes it behind the classic _disposed guard (line 356). Every async handler swallows OperationCanceledException silently (for example lines 251-254) because that is the expected outcome when the user navigates away mid-fetch.
      • Result-typed failures, not exceptions. The service calls return a Result, so the page branches on TryGetValue (line 229) and routes the failure through result.NotifyOnFailure(Toast, L) (line 248). A failure now has two surfaces: the toast, and the last outcome kept in _loadResult (line 62) for an inline ErrorSummary plus a Retry button. The list is left as it was rather than blanked, so a transient failure does not erase what is on screen.
      • Busy flags gate the UI. IsLoading and IsSaving (lines 54-55) are protected with private setters; the markup shows progress while loading and sets Disabled="IsSaving" on the action controls (NotificationInbox.razor:18) so a double click cannot double-post.
      • Push-driven refresh via an event subscription. OnInitializedAsync subscribes to NotificationState.OnRefreshRequested (line 89) and Dispose(bool) unsubscribes (line 364).
      • [Rubric §19, State Management & Data Flow] assesses where state lives; transient view state stays in private fields (_notifications, _currentPage, _totalPages, _loadResult, lines 57-62) while the shared unread count is written back into the scoped NotificationState (lines 309, 343) and its refresh signal is read. Local stays local, shared stays shared.
      • [Rubric §25, Navigation, Routing & Information Architecture] assesses route structure. The second @page directive is a typed deep link: a push payload or an email can point straight at one notification. The class doc (lines 19-25) states the two design rules that follow from it: the :int route constraint is the validation boundary, so a malformed id never reaches the component (the router renders NotFound instead), and an id that is simply not on the loaded page degrades silently to the plain inbox rather than raising an error the user can do nothing about.
      • [Rubric §21, Accessibility]: the icon-only mark-read control carries an explicit localized aria-label (NotificationInbox.razor:66).
      • [Rubric §27, Internationalization & Localization]: this page holds no literal English. The injected IStringLocalizer<SharedResource> L (line 34) resolves the title (line 50), the breadcrumbs, and every toast (L["Notif.AllMarkedRead"], line 344). The breadcrumb trail is built inside OnInitializedAsync (from line 79), not in a field initializer, so the injected localizer is available and labels re-resolve per circuit under the active culture (comment in that method, citing ADR-027).
    • Walkthrough
      • PageSize (line 30) is const int 20: fixed-size server-side pagination, not infinite scroll. Injected InboxService, NotificationState, Toast, L, MudBlazor's ScrollManager, and ViewerTime (lines 32-37).
      • [Parameter] public int? Id (line 46) is the deep-link route parameter. The doc (lines 39-45) explains the type choice: UserNotificationIdentifierType is an int alias, and a route parameter's type must be written out for the :int constraint to bind, so the parameter is declared int? and converted where it is used.
      • Deep-link state is four separate fields, and each exists for a distinct reason (lines 67-77): _highlightedId (found on the loaded page), _pendingScrollId (a scroll the next render owes), _scrolledId (already scrolled, so a re-render or push-driven reload never scrolls twice), and _appliedId (the Id the state was last computed for, to detect a re-navigation).
      • OnParametersSet (lines 100-109) clears the _scrolledId latch when _appliedId != Id and then recomputes the target. The doc (lines 94-99) records the bug this prevents: navigating from /notifications/inbox/5 to /notifications/inbox/9 reuses the component instance, so without clearing the latch the second deep link would highlight but never move the viewport.
      • OnAfterRenderAsync (lines 112-130) first resolves the viewer's time zone: on the first render, while the component is alive, it awaits ViewerTime.EnsureResolvedAsync(_cts.LifetimeToken()) and calls StateHasChanged when the zone changed (lines 114-118), because sent times render on the viewer's clock and the zone is only readable once JS is available (comment above line 114). It is also the only place a scroll happens. It returns unless a scroll is pending and the component is alive, clears _pendingScrollId and sets _scrolledId before the await (comment, line 125, so a re-entrant render cannot queue the same scroll twice), and calls ScrollManager.ScrollIntoViewAsync(CardSelector(id), ScrollBehavior.Smooth) (line 129).
      • ApplyDeepLinkTarget (lines 138-152) matches the route id against what the loaded page actually holds: Id is not { } id || id <= 0 || !_notifications.Exists(n => n.Id == id) clears both the highlight and the pending scroll (lines 140-145). The doc (lines 132-137) is the "no toast" decision, a deep link the user cannot act on is not an error they caused.
      • The card-chrome helpers: IsDeepLinkTarget (line 154); CardElementId (lines 156-159, formatting notification-{id} with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture because it becomes a DOM id) and CardSelector (line 161); CardElevation (from line 164, 4 when deep-linked, else 1 for unread and 0 for read); CardClass (from line 181), which emits only state classes (notification-card, read or unread, plus deep-linked). The chrome those classes select lives in wwwroot/app.css (.notification-card.unread and .notification-card.deep-linked, app.css:519,523), built from MudBlazor palette tokens only so both themes stay legible: a primary left border marks unread, a secondary-colored ring plus a faint surface tint marks the deep link (doc above CardClass). [Rubric §20, Design System & Theming] shows up here: the page builds no inline styles, so its colors come from the theme's tokens in one stylesheet.
      • Push coalescing. HandleRefreshRequested (lines 189-197) is EventHandler-shaped so it cannot be async Task; it discards into InvokeAsync(RefreshFromPushAsync) (line 196). RefreshFromPushAsync (lines 199-216) sets _refreshPending = true and returns when a load is already in flight (from line 206); the comment beside it states the invariant, never drop the push, so overlapping pushes coalesce into exactly one trailing reload instead of vanishing.
      • LoadNotificationsAsync (lines 218-274) returns Task<bool> (true when the page loaded) and starts by setting IsLoading (line 223). It clears _loadResult, calls GetInboxAsync(_currentPage, PageSize, _cts.LifetimeToken()) (line 227) and stores the outcome in _loadResult (line 228) so the markup can show a failure inline. On success (line 229) it materializes page.Items, computes _totalPages from page.PaginationMetadata.TotalItemCount with Math.Ceiling (line 233) clamped to a floor of 1 so an empty inbox never renders a zero-page pager, then recomputes the deep-link highlight (only a successful load can decide whether the id is present). A failure goes through result.NotifyOnFailure(Toast, L) (line 248). The tail (from line 263) drains _refreshPending with one more RefreshFromPushAsync; the flag is cleared first (line 265), so a push arriving during this reload queues one more and no further.
      • OnPageChangedAsync(int page) (lines 276-284): remembers the previous page (line 278), records the new one, reloads, and restores the previous page number when the load failed (lines 280-282), because a failed load keeps the previous page's rows on screen and the pager must point back at the page those rows belong to.
      • MarkReadAsync(UserNotificationDTO) (lines 286-320): calls MarkReadAsync(notification.Id, _cts.LifetimeToken()) (line 291), returns early on failure after a toast, then optimistically patches local state, locating the row with FindIndex (line 299) and replacing it via a record with-expression, notification with { IsRead = true, ReadOn = DateTime.UtcNow } (line 302). It then refetches the authoritative unread count (line 306) and pushes it into NotificationState.SetUnreadCount only when the count call succeeded (lines 307-310); a failed count means "unknown", so the badge keeps its value.
      • MarkAllReadAsync (lines 322-354): one service call (line 327), a loop flipping every unread row in place (line 339), then SetUnreadCount(0) (line 343) and a localized success toast (line 344).
      • Disposal: _disposed (line 356), Dispose(bool) (lines 358-370) unsubscribing the refresh event (line 364) and cancelling the _cts (line 365), Dispose() (lines 372-376) with GC.SuppressFinalize (line 375).
    • Why it's built this way: the page is a thin view over INotificationInboxUIService, so all HTTP and JSON live in the service and the component stays testable against a stub. Patching local state after a mark-read (rather than refetching the page) keeps the interaction snappy while still reconciling the shared badge from the server, and the coalescing refresh keeps the list current when pushes arrive in bursts. The deep-link machinery is worth reading as a case study in idempotent side effects: a scroll is a one-shot action in a component model that re-renders freely, so it needs the "owed" and "already done" flags to be correct under re-render, re-navigation, and disposal.
    • Where it's used: rendered at /notifications/inbox (and /notifications/inbox/{Id:int}) for authenticated users; the route constant and nav entry come from NotificationRoutePaths and NotificationUIModule. NotificationBell reads the same NotificationState this page writes, and the layout-mounted NotificationListener raises the OnRefreshRequested signal it consumes. Its admin siblings are NotificationList and NotificationSend.

    • What it is: the code-behind for the admin/organizer push-notification history page, routed at @page "/notifications" (NotificationList.razor:1). It loads previously sent broadcasts and renders them in a status table (title, recipients, status, phone delivery, sent time; NotificationList.razor:70-74), with a button onward to the compose page. It renders only for an account holding the notifications:manage permission claim; any other account gets the 403 view and the history endpoint is never called (field comment, lines 36-39).
    • Depends on: first-party: IPushNotificationUIService (the send and history HTTP service), PushNotificationDTO (the row shape, carrying status, recipient count, and the per-platform native counts AndroidSent, AndroidFailed, AppleSent, AppleFailed plus NativeDeliveryUnit, MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Notifications/PushNotifications/PushNotificationDTO.cs:32-47), PhoneDeliveryLine (its private phone-cell line record), NotificationRoutePaths (the route constants), IToastService, ResultUiExtensions (NotifyOnFailure), and SharedResource. Externals: MudBlazor (BreadcrumbItem, Icons, Color), Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components (NavigationManager, [Inject]), Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.
    • Concept reinforced, the same code-behind shape as NotificationInbox. Same [Inject] service set (lines 26-30), same readonly CancellationTokenSource _cts plus dispose pattern (lines 34, 192-211), same IsLoading gate (line 45), same cancellation-swallowing load, same result.NotifyOnFailure(Toast, L) failure surface (line 162), same Task<bool> load plus revert-on-failure OnPageChangedAsync, and the same inline _loadResult outcome. It differs mainly in what it loads and who may see it.
      • [Rubric §25, Navigation, Routing & Information Architecture] assesses route structure and inter-page flow; navigation goes through NotificationRoutePaths constants (NavigateToSend targets NotificationRoutePaths.NotificationSend, line 190) rather than a literal URL, so a route change happens in exactly one file.
      • [Rubric §27, Internationalization & Localization] picks up an extra trick here: DisplayStatus(string status) (lines 55-59) looks up L[$"Notif.Status.{status}"] and falls back to the raw wire value when localized.ResourceNotFound (line 58). The comparison value stays the untranslated wire string while only the displayed chip text localizes, which keeps transport values and presentation separate and means a newly added server status renders (untranslated) instead of blanking (the comment above it cites ADR-027). This is the same pass-through-on-unknown-key discipline that DataAnnotationsModelValidator applies to error messages. The phone column applies it once more to the delivery unit: the unit word is looked up as Notif.Phone.Unit.{unit}.One or .Other, chosen by whether the attempted count is 1, and an unknown unit name drops the word (the Notif.Phone.LineNoUnit format) rather than show a raw key (lines 92-97).
      • Concept introduced, the per-platform native delivery outcome (ADR-044). Each history row shows, per platform the native (OS-level) leg counted, a status-first line with the unit explicit, for example "Android: delivered (1 of 1 batch)" (doc comment, lines 61-66). The point is operator feedback: a sender learns whether the phones actually received the broadcast, not only how many recipients were addressed. The status is derived from two nullable counts, so a platform with neither count recorded contributes no line, and a recorded unit with no per-platform counts at all is shown as one "Phones: failed" line, because that is a failure the sender could not attribute to a platform (FCM) (lines 63-65, 72-76). Each line is a PhoneDeliveryLine whose text, not only its chip color and icon, carries the status ([Rubric §21, Accessibility]).

      • _notifications is an IReadOnlyCollection<PushNotificationDTO> initialized empty (line 47), alongside the paging state _currentPage and _totalPages (lines 48-49) and the last outcome _loadResult (line 52).
      • PhoneDeliveryLines(PushNotificationDTO) (lines 67-79) builds the phone cell for one row: it calls AddPhoneDeliveryLine for Android and then Apple with that platform's sent and failed counts and the row's NativeDeliveryUnit (lines 70-71), and when neither produced a line but a unit was recorded it adds the single error line from Notif.Phone.StatusOnly (lines 72-76). An empty list renders as - (NotificationList.razor:100-103). AddPhoneDeliveryLine (lines 81-99) returns when both counts are null, takes delivered = sent ?? 0 and attempted = delivered + (failed ?? 0) (lines 88-89), and formats the line. PhoneDeliveryStatus (lines 101-111) maps the two counts to a status key, color and icon: Notif.Phone.Delivered when attempted == delivered, otherwise Notif.Phone.PartlyFailed when anything was delivered and Notif.Phone.Failed when nothing was.
      • OnInitializedAsync (lines 116-133) first reads the cascading auth state and sets _canManage = user.HasPermissionClaim(NotificationPermissions.Manage) (lines 118-119); when it is false it returns before building breadcrumbs or loading anything (lines 120-123), so the 403 view never triggers the history call. Otherwise it builds the breadcrumbs then awaits LoadNotificationsAsync (line 132). OnAfterRenderAsync (lines 136-143) resolves the viewer's time zone on the first render through ViewerTime.EnsureResolvedAsync(_cts.LifetimeToken()) and re-renders when it changed, because sent times render on the viewer's clock and the zone is only readable once JS is available.
      • LoadNotificationsAsync (lines 147-174) returns Task<bool> and loads one server page: GetHistoryAsync(_currentPage, PageSize, _cts.LifetimeToken()) (line 153) with PageSize 20 (line 24). It stores the outcome in _loadResult (line 154) for inline rendering, copies history.Items into _notifications on success and sets _totalPages to Math.Max(1, ceiling(TotalItemCount / PageSize)) (line 158), then returns true; on failure it raises the localized toast (line 162) and returns false. OnPageChangedAsync (lines 180-188) records the page, reloads, and restores the previous _currentPage when the load failed (lines 184-187), so the pager stays on the page whose rows are still shown.
      • NavigateToSend (line 190) sends the "send new" button to the compose page.
      • Disposal mirrors the family: _disposed (line 192), Dispose(bool) cancelling the _cts (lines 194-205), Dispose() (lines 207-211).
    • Why it's built this way: broadcast history is paged on the server, 20 rows at a time (PageSize, line 24), so the page never holds more than one window, and a failed load keeps the previous rows on screen while the pager reverts. Keeping HTTP behind IPushNotificationUIService mirrors the inbox and keeps the component a thin view. The shared [Rubric §18, UI Architecture & Component Design] story is told under NotificationInbox.
    • Where it's used: rendered at /notifications for accounts holding the notifications:manage permission (the nav entry from NotificationUIModule carries RequiredPermission: NotificationPermissions.Manage, NotificationUIModule.cs:20); it links onward to NotificationSend.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the page size (PageSize, 20, line 24) is a client-side constant in this file; any server-side cap on pageSize is not visible here.

All four are present: model-declared rules run through the shared delegate, an IsSaving flag (line 44) bound to Disabled on both buttons (NotificationSend.razor:73,80) so the send cannot be fired twice (backed in code by a re-entrancy guard, _form is null || IsSaving, raised before the first await at lines 109-113: each send mints its own idempotency key, so a second click that slipped in while the first was still validating would broadcast twice), a warning toast ErrorMessages.ValidationError on a failed gate (line 127), and a success toast naming the recipient count (line 137).
      • Two failure surfaces, deliberately not one. _sendResult (line 53) holds the last attempt's outcome and is rendered inline by the shared ErrorSummary component (NotificationSend.razor:36), while the toast stays the transient cue. The markup comment (lines 31-35) records the design constraint: the summary is deliberately not fed MudForm.Errors, because every field already renders its own message inline and MudBlazor contributes a generic "Required" of its own that would stack on top of the model's wording. The code repeats the point at the failed-validation branch (comment, lines 125-126): the per-field messages are already on screen, the ErrorSummary is deliberately not fed them, so the snackbar stays the summary cue. _sendResult is nulled at the start of every attempt (line 118), so the summary never shows a stale failure.
      • [Rubric §21, Accessibility] and [Rubric §18, UI Architecture & Component Design] meet in the ErrorSummary: a failure that only appeared as a toast would time out on a long form and be unrecoverable for a screen-reader user who missed it (comment, lines 146-147).

As with its siblings the breadcrumb trail is built in an initialization hook, here the synchronous OnInitialized (lines 66-78, comment citing ADR-027).
      • [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety] again, for the navigate-away guard: Sent (a private bool, set true immediately before the post-send NavigateTo) and IsDirty (true whenever Sent is false and either field is non-blank) feed the markup's UnsavedChangesGuard, so leaving with typed-but-unsent text prompts, while the send's own redirect never does. The comment on the Sent setter records the ordering: it is set before the navigation call, because the guard reads the live accessor.

The field doc (lines 59-64) and the comment (lines 89-92) give the reasoning: a scoped application applies its scope to the send automatically, so without a caption the operator would be composing a broadcast with no visible statement of who receives it, and when there is no scope the page renders no caption at all rather than an empty line. On a non-null PushNotificationDTO it raises the success toast with sent.RecipientCount (line 137), sets Sent = true (line 141), and navigates back to the list; otherwise result.NotifyOnFailure(Toast, L) (line 148). The rules live on NotificationSendModel so the client cap, the client message, and the server invariant all read the same constants; HTTP stays behind IPushNotificationUIService so the component is unit-testable; and the Sent/IsDirty pair keeps the unsaved-changes guard from firing on the page's own post-send redirect, which is the one navigation on this page that is not the user abandoning work.     ColumnFilterState

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/ColumnFilterState.cs:10 · Level 0 · record (sealed, positional)

    • What it is: one saved grid column filter, reduced to the two strings a list page needs to put it back: the MudDataGrid operator and the filter value (ColumnFilterState.cs:10).
    • Depends on: nothing. It is a leaf value carried inside ListPageState.
    • Concept introduced, persisting a vendor filter as plain strings. [Rubric §19, State Management & Data Flow] assesses whether UI state can cross every boundary it has to cross. A MudDataGrid filter definition is a live object bound to a grid column, so it cannot travel through sessionStorage JSON or a URL; this record is the transport-neutral form of it. The summary (ColumnFilterState.cs:3-7) fixes the two rules that make the round trip deterministic: the value is written in the invariant culture, and it is null for an operator that takes no value (is empty).
    • Walkthrough
      • Operator is the MudDataGrid operator text, for example contains or >= (ColumnFilterState.cs:4-5, parameter doc at ColumnFilterState.cs:8).
      • Value is the invariant-culture value or null (ColumnFilterState.cs:9).
      • The grid page builds one per effective column filter through new ColumnFilterState(definition.Operator!, FormatFilterValue(definition.Value)) (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DataGridListPageBase.ColumnFilters.cs:92-95).
      • ListPageQueryStateService writes it to the URL as c:<property>=<operator>:<value> and parses it back, mapping an empty value after the colon to null (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/ListPageQueryStateService.cs:256-268).
    • Why it's built this way: a positional sealed record gives value equality, so two snapshots of the same filters compare equal, and JSON serialization for the sessionStorage tier with no custom converter. Keeping the value a string (not an object) means the same shape works for text, number, date and enum columns; the grid page re-parses it against the column type on restore, and a value that no longer parses is dropped rather than sent to the API (DataGridListPageBase.ColumnFilters.cs:17-18).
    • Where it's used: the ColumnFilters member of ListPageState (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/ListPageStateService.cs:59), the saved dictionary in DataGridListPageBase<TDto> (DataGridListPageBase.ColumnFilters.cs:22) and the c: codec in ListPageQueryStateService (ListPageQueryStateService.cs:191-220).     LazyJsModule

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/LazyJsModule.cs:20 · Level 0 · class (internal sealed)

    • What it is: a small single-flight importer that owns one JavaScript module reference for a UI service: it imports on first use, shares one import across concurrent callers, and disposes the reference safely when the circuit ends.
    • Depends on: Microsoft.JSInterop (IJSRuntime, IJSObjectReference, JSDisconnectedException) and the .NET System.Threading.Lock type. No first-party dependencies.
    • Concept introduced, single-flight JS module import. [Rubric §23, Front-End Performance] assesses whether the client loads only what it needs, when it needs it; deferring import() until first use is the lazy half of that, and collapsing concurrent imports into one is the correctness half. The class comment (LazyJsModule.cs:5-13) states the exact defect this replaces: an unguarded _module ??= await import(...) lets two concurrent callers each start an import, after which the browser holds two module instances and the later assignment leaks the earlier reference, which is never disposed. [Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality] applies to the second half of the design: a failed import is dropped rather than cached, so an import attempted during SSR prerender (when JS interop does not exist yet) does not poison the module for the rest of the circuit.
    • Walkthrough
      • The primary constructor takes the IJSRuntime and the module path (LazyJsModule.cs:20). State is three fields: a Lock (LazyJsModule.cs:22), the in-flight import task (LazyJsModule.cs:24) and the resolved module (LazyJsModule.cs:25). IsImported (LazyJsModule.cs:28) exists so disposal can skip work.
      • GetOrImportAsync (LazyJsModule.cs:37) starts with a lock-free fast path returning the cached module (LazyJsModule.cs:39-42), then takes the lock only to publish or read the in-flight task (LazyJsModule.cs:47-51); the inline comment (LazyJsModule.cs:44-45) notes why holding a lock there is safe, since ImportAsync reaches its first await immediately and nothing slow runs under it. The import is started with no caller token at all (LazyJsModule.cs:49), and each caller then awaits the shared task through WaitAsync(cancellationToken) (LazyJsModule.cs:55), so a caller's token cancels only that caller's wait, never the import. The method summary (LazyJsModule.cs:30-36) gives the reason: binding the import to the first caller's token would let that one caller's cancellation fault the import for every concurrent awaiter.
      • The finally block is the subtle part (LazyJsModule.cs:57-73): it clears the field only when the task has completed and did not complete successfully (LazyJsModule.cs:63), and only when the field still holds this task (LazyJsModule.cs:67), because clearing unconditionally could drop a newer import started after this one completed and split the next set of callers. The inline comment (LazyJsModule.cs:59-62) covers the cancellation case: a caller that stopped waiting on its own token leaves the import still running rather than failed, so it stays cached for the others.
      • ImportAsync (LazyJsModule.cs:76-86) performs the actual js.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("import", CancellationToken.None, modulePath) (LazyJsModule.cs:79-81) and assigns _module (LazyJsModule.cs:84). The call sits inside a #pragma warning disable BL0016 pair (LazyJsModule.cs:78 and LazyJsModule.cs:82), and the justification on the disable line is the design point: a failed import must fault the shared task, so GetOrImportAsync evicts it and every awaiting caller observes the failure.
      • DisposeAsync (LazyJsModule.cs:89-106) returns immediately when nothing was imported (LazyJsModule.cs:91-94), nulls the field before awaiting (LazyJsModule.cs:96), and swallows JSDisconnectedException (LazyJsModule.cs:102-105), since a torn-down circuit is the normal end of life for a scoped UI service.
    • Why it's built this way: the remarks (LazyJsModule.cs:14-19) draw the responsibility line. This class deliberately does not swallow anything on the import path, so each consuming service keeps its own degradation contract (return a default, fall back to a navigation, no-op). That is why ListPageStateService wraps its calls in catch-and-ignore blocks while MmcaCultureBootstrap, which does not use this type at all, imports its module directly under an await using.
    • Where it's used: ThemeService (ThemeService.cs:26), ListPageStateService (ListPageStateService.cs:76), NavigationHistoryService (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Navigation/NavigationHistoryService.cs:16) CapabilitiesJsModule (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Capabilities/CapabilitiesJsModule.cs:19), BrowserPasskeyCapability (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Capabilities/Auth/BrowserPasskeyCapability.cs:26), ViewerTimeZone (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Culture/ViewerTimeZone.cs:30), PendingToastService (PendingToastService.cs:20), AppLockInertBackground (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Capabilities/AppLockInertBackground.cs:20) and InfiniteScrollObserver<TOwner> (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Lists/InfiniteScrollObserver.cs:27). Pinned by MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/LazyJsModuleTests.cs.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: it is internal (LazyJsModule.cs:20), so it is not part of the published package surface: consumer apps get the benefit through the services that use it, not by using it directly.

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/QueryStringCodec.cs:27 · Level 0 · class (internal static)

    • What it is: the package's own URL query-string reader and writer, behaving like ASP.NET Core's QueryHelpers.ParseQuery and QueryHelpers.AddQueryString without taking the Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebUtilities package (QueryStringCodec.cs:7-11).
    • Depends on: BCL only: StringBuilder, UrlEncoder.Default, Uri.UnescapeDataString and StringValues from Microsoft.Extensions.Primitives (QueryStringCodec.cs:1-3).
    • Concept introduced, owning a small helper instead of a server dependency. [Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality] assesses whether a dependency earns its weight. The summary (QueryStringCodec.cs:10) gives the reason this one did not: the UI project stays WebAssembly-safe and carries no ASP.NET Core server dependency, so the two query-string operations the list pages need are owned here instead. The remarks (QueryStringCodec.cs:12-26) spell out the exact parsing and building rules, so the behavior is a documented contract rather than "whatever the old helper did".
    • Walkthrough
      • Parse (QueryStringCodec.cs:32-60) skips one leading ? (QueryStringCodec.cs:36-39), splits on & only and skips empty segments (QueryStringCodec.cs:41-51), accumulating into a case-insensitive (StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) dictionary of lists (QueryStringCodec.cs:34). It then folds each list into a StringValues, single-valued when the key appeared once (QueryStringCodec.cs:53-57), so a repeated key keeps every value in order.
      • The private Append (QueryStringCodec.cs:98-111) ends the key at the first = and treats a segment with no = as a key with an empty value (QueryStringCodec.cs:100-102). Decode (QueryStringCodec.cs:113-114) turns + into a space before percent-decoding, matching form encoding.
      • AddQueryString (QueryStringCodec.cs:69-95) splits off any #fragment first (QueryStringCodec.cs:74-76) so the pairs land before it, starts with ? unless the URI already has a query (QueryStringCodec.cs:77 and QueryStringCodec.cs:87), skips a pair whose value is null (QueryStringCodec.cs:82-85), and encodes both key and value with UrlEncoder.Default (QueryStringCodec.cs:88-90).
    • Why it's built this way: a # is deliberately not special on the parse side, so a caller passes the query part only (QueryStringCodec.cs:18-19), which is what Uri.Query already gives ListPageQueryStateService. The parse walks the input as a ReadOnlySpan<char> (QueryStringCodec.cs:35) and allocates strings only for decoded keys and values.
    • Where it's used: only by ListPageQueryStateService, in ParseQueryString (ListPageQueryStateService.cs:65) and BuildPath (ListPageQueryStateService.cs:155). Pinned by MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/QueryStringCodecTests.cs.

    ListPageState

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/ListPageStateService.cs:9 · Level 1 · record (sealed)

    • What it is: the immutable snapshot of everything a list page needs to look the same after you navigate away and come back: which page, how many rows, how far down, which sort, which density, which named filters and which grid column filters.
    • Depends on: ColumnFilterState for its column-filter entries. It is the currency shared by ListPageStateService (in-memory plus sessionStorage), ListPageQueryStateService (URL encoding) and DataGridListPageBase<TDto> (the consumer).
    • Concept introduced, one state shape over three transports. [Rubric §19, State Management & Data Flow] assesses whether UI state has a single defined shape rather than being reconstructed ad hoc per page; this record is that shape, and the fact that memory, session storage and the address bar all move the same record is what keeps the three from drifting. The record is documented as update-by-with (ListPageStateService.cs:5-7), so a caller changing scroll position cannot accidentally reset paging.
    • Walkthrough
      • Nine init members, all with defaults, so new ListPageState() is a valid pristine state.
      • Page (ListPageStateService.cs:12) is the MudDataGrid 0-indexed page; PageSize (ListPageStateService.cs:15) the chosen rows per page; MobilePage (ListPageStateService.cs:18) the 1-indexed card-list page, and it is the only member with a non-default default (= 1), because a mobile page zero does not exist.
      • ScrollPosition (ListPageStateService.cs:26) is a double of pixels, and its doc comment (ListPageStateService.cs:20-25) names which element it measures: the document (document.scrollingElement.scrollTop) for a normal paged list page, and the grid's own height-bound viewport (.mud-table-container) for a page that opts into grid virtualization, where the document itself does not scroll.
      • SortColumn (ListPageStateService.cs:32) holds the SortBy property name of the active sort definition and is null or empty when unsorted; SortDescending (ListPageStateService.cs:38) is documented as ignored when it is.
      • DenseGrid (ListPageStateService.cs:46) carries the compact-density opt-in, persisted alongside paging and sort so the chosen density survives navigation, refresh and shared links.
      • Filters (ListPageStateService.cs:52) is an IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> of page-specific named values (the doc gives "search" and "status" as examples) defaulting to an empty dictionary, so each page decides what it saves.
      • ColumnFilters (ListPageStateService.cs:59) is an IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ColumnFilterState> keyed by the column's property name, also defaulting to empty. Its doc comment (ListPageStateService.cs:54-58) draws the contrast with Filters: the base list page saves and restores these itself, so a column filter survives opening a row and coming back, a refresh and a shared link without any per-page code.
    • Why it's built this way: a sealed record gives value equality and with-based copies for free, which is what makes the "update only scroll position" and "update only density" paths in the services one-liners.
    • Where it's used: produced and consumed by both list-page state services and by DataGridListPageBase<TDto> (DataGridListPageBase.cs:745-747, where a non-empty ColumnFilters also counts as restorable state, and DataGridListPageBase.cs:749); serialized to sessionStorage as JSON and encoded into the query string. The column-filter half is read back by RestoreColumnFilters (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DataGridListPageBase.ColumnFilters.cs:29-32).

A bUnit test pins the registration to this implementation (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Infrastructure/BunitComponentTestBaseFacadeTests.cs:32).

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/PendingToastService.cs:76 · Level 1 · record (internal sealed, nested in PendingToastService)

    • What it is: the stored payload of a parked toast, a two-field record of a ToastSeverity and the message text (PendingToastService.cs:76). It is the shape written to and read from sessionStorage.
    • Depends on: ToastSeverity only.
    • Walkthrough
      • The doc comment (line 75) states the wire format: JS interop serializes it camelCase as { severity, message }.
      • PendingToastService constructs it on the write path (PendingToastService.cs:33) and asks interop to deserialize into PendingToast? on the read path (PendingToastService.cs:47).
