    BlazorWebHostExtensions

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Hosting · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Hosting/BlazorWebHostExtensions.cs:44 · Level 6 · class (static)

    • What it is: the composed Blazor web host: the shared registration list, the shared request pipeline and the shared additional-assembly list every Blazor Server + WebAssembly head repeats, as three calls (class doc, BlazorWebHostExtensions.cs:32-39). What differs arrives through MmcaBlazorWebHostOptions and MmcaBlazorWebPipelineOptions.
    • Depends on: ApiEndpointUrl, BlazorCircuitLimitExtensions, UiRateLimitingExtensions, SessionCookieAuthenticationHandler, IForbiddenReExecutionDetector / HttpContextForbiddenReExecutionDetector, ITokenRefresher / SameOriginProxyTokenRefresher, SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions, SameOriginApiProxyEndpointExtensions, JwtAuthenticationStateProvider, AuthenticatedNoStoreExtensions, ClientConfigEndpointExtensions, ServiceWorkerEndpointExtensions, IUIModule, and AddCommonSerilog (SerilogHostExtensions). Externals: MudBlazor AddMudServices, Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience ResilienceHandler, ASP.NET Core antiforgery, authentication and static assets.
    • Concept introduced, the composed host. A Blazor head's host setup is a long registration and middleware list whose ordering matters (configuration sources before anything reads configuration, the proxy refresher after token storage, the rate limiter ahead of the exception handler). Holding that list in one framework call fixes the order once and leaves the head only the values that genuinely differ, passed as callbacks that run at named positions. Render-mode registration deliberately stays per head (ConfigureRazorComponents, DevelopmentPipeline and the head's own MapRazorComponents chain), so the package takes no WebAssembly server dependency (:36-38). [Rubric §33, Developer Experience] assesses how much a team repeats to stand up a component; here a head's host is three calls plus options. [Rubric §18, UI Architecture] assesses whether UI composition is consistent across apps; the shared pipeline and assembly list are that consistency. See ADR-079 and ADR-067.
    • Walkthrough
      • ApiEndpointKey (:46): "Api:ApiEndpoint".
      • AddMmcaBlazorWebHost(MmcaBlazorWebHostOptions) (:75), in extension(WebApplicationBuilder builder) (:48). In order: ConfigureConfigurationSources (:82, first so a vault value is visible to everything below); AddCommonSerilog(options.LogFilePath) (:84); AddServiceDefaults() (:85); AfterServiceDefaults (:86); AddRazorComponents().AddInteractiveServerComponents(...) with the circuit retention read from configuration, then ConfigureRazorComponents (:91-93); bounded circuits and the UI rate limiter (:95-96, ADR-124, ADR-019); MudBlazor with or without the callback (:98-105); AddUIShared, then the private resilience-handler removal, then browser device capabilities (:107-109).
      • The API endpoint guard (:114-121): Api:ApiEndpoint must be an absolute http(s) URL or an Aspire service-discovery name (ApiEndpointUrl.IsAbsoluteHttpOrServiceDiscovery), otherwise InvalidOperationException, so a deployment placeholder fails at boot rather than at the first call.
      • Auth and session (:123-130): the server and client session-cookie pair, the trusted-caller header, session-cookie authentication as the default scheme (ADR-022) and the authorization policies with the head's fallback callback.
      • Token flow (:134-142): server token storage, then AddHttpContextAccessor and a Replace of IForbiddenReExecutionDetector with the request-reading HttpContextForbiddenReExecutionDetector (only this server host can see a 403 re-executed to /not-found, :136-139), then ITokenRefresher as SameOriginProxyTokenRefresher and the same-origin API proxy. The proxy is registered after token storage because it replaces the circuit's ITokenRefresher and ISessionCookieSync (:132-133); the summary (:63-66) warns a head not to register either afterward, since MapCommonSameOriginApiProxy fails the boot when displaced (ADR-051).
      • Tail (:144-158): JwtAuthenticationStateProvider, cascading auth state, the distributed memory cache, the web form factor, antiforgery with CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest (:154; the comment at :149-153 explains why not Always: it would refuse tokens on any request seen as http, such as a local container or a probe), then the dynamic Blazor CSP before the security headers whose static default is a TryAdd (:157-158, ADR-023).
      • UseMmcaBlazorWebPipeline(MmcaBlazorWebPipelineOptions? = null) (:181), in extension(WebApplication app) (:164): forwarded headers, security headers, the UI rate limiter (ahead of the exception handler so a throttled request answers 429 without re-rendering a page, :166-169) (:185-187); the Development callback or UseExceptionHandler("/Error", createScopeForErrors: true) (:189-196); UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/not-found") (:198); MapDefaultEndpoints, HTTPS redirection, request localization, antiforgery, UseAuthenticatedNoStore, cookie session refresh, authentication, authorization (:199-206); then the client-config endpoint with the head's extras, session-cookie endpoints, the same-origin proxy, the culture endpoint, MapStaticAssets().AllowAnonymous() and the service worker (:208-213).
      • GetMmcaRazorComponentAssemblies(Assembly clientAssembly) (:225): MMCA.Common.UI, MMCA.Common.UI.Web (the shared SSR error page) and the client assembly (:230-235), concatenated with the Assembly of every registered IUIModule and de-duplicated keeping the first occurrence (:240-241).
      • RemoveApiClientResilienceHandler (:260, private): walks the "APIClient" handler list backward through ConfigureAdditionalHttpMessageHandlers and removes every ResilienceHandler (:264-269). The remarks (:246-259) give the reason: the standard handler's 30 s attempt timeout with POST never retried cut large uploads off in Server mode, where the body streams from the browser over the circuit; removing it leaves one HttpClient.Timeout of HttpResilienceDefaults.TotalRequestTimeout (90 s, set by AddUIShared) as in WebAssembly and MAUI. RemoveAllResilienceHandlers() is avoided because it is still EXTEXP0001 (experimental).
    • Why it's built this way: the order comments in the body are the reason the call exists: each "X before Y" rule is enforced once in the framework instead of in every head. Callbacks rather than overridable registrations keep a head from reordering. The CA1708 suppression on the class (:40-43) is a documented false positive from having two extension(T) blocks in one static class (ADR-106).
    • Where it's used: MMCA.ADC.UI.Web's Program.cs is the three calls: builder.AddMmcaBlazorWebHost(new() { ... }) (MMCA.ADC/Source/Hosts/UI/MMCA.ADC.UI.Web/Program.cs:26), app.UseMmcaBlazorWebPipeline(...) (:128, :130) and .AddAdditionalAssemblies(app.GetMmcaRazorComponentAssemblies(...)) on its own MapRazorComponents<App>() chain (:165), with its app-association endpoints mapped in between as the pipeline summary prescribes (BlazorWebHostExtensions.cs:174-177). Tests: BlazorWebHostExtensionsTests, BlazorWebPipelineTests and BlazorWebHostHarness under MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/Hosting/.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: whether MMCA.Store's head also uses the composed calls is not determinable from this unit's evidence (only MMCA.Common and MMCA.ADC were searched; the LogFilePath doc example names a Store log file).

    • Depends on: nothing first-party.
    • Concept: a wire DTO for an opaque, Data-Protection-sealed token; the sealing is taught on SessionHandoffProtector.
    • Walkthrough: the token endpoint returns it with a protected access token (SessionHandoffEndpoints.cs:41); the cookie endpoint binds it from the request body and unprotects body.Handoff (SessionHandoffEndpoints.cs:49,56).
    • Why it's built this way: the property is nullable so a missing or empty body binds instead of failing model binding; the protector then treats null or whitespace as "no handoff" (SessionHandoffProtector.cs:59-62) and the endpoint answers 400 invalid_handoff (SessionHandoffEndpoints.cs:57-60).
    • Where it's used: only inside SessionHandoffEndpoints.cs.

    ProxyResponseMode

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SameOriginProxyTransformer.cs:16 · Level 0 · enum

    • What it is: how the same-origin proxy treats the upstream response of one forwarded request: Forward (copy as is), TokenIssuing (a sign-in: move the token pair into the session cookies and strip it from the body), Revoke (a sign-out: copy, then clear the session cookies), ViewAsGrant (a view-as grant, ADR-137: move the token into the overlay cookie and strip it from the body, leaving the session cookies alone) and ViewAsEnd (end of a view-as session: copy, then delete the overlay cookie) (SameOriginProxyTransformer.cs:19,22,25,31,34).
    • Depends on: nothing first-party.
    • Concept: a strategy selector passed into the per-request SameOriginProxyTransformer; see that section for each mode's mechanism.
    • Walkthrough: SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint picks the mode in ResolveMode (SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint.cs:313-347): every non-POST is Forward; a POST to the refresh path yields null (the proxy answers it itself); a POST to a token-issuing path is TokenIssuing; a POST to either sign-out path (RevokePath or RevokeCurrentPath) is Revoke (:330-335); a POST to ViewAsEndPath is ViewAsEnd (:337-340); a POST whose last segment is view-as is ViewAsGrant (:342-346); any other POST is Forward.
    • Why it's built this way: the endpoint decides once per request and the transformer branches on it (SameOriginProxyTransformer.cs:81,106,113,118), so the request path matching stays in one class and the body rewriting in another.
    • Where it's used: SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint and SameOriginProxyTransformer only; it is internal.

    SameOriginApiProxyMarker

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions.cs:92 · Level 0 · class

    • What it is: an empty internal sealed class registered as a singleton only by AddCommonSameOriginApiProxy (SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions.cs:81,92), so other code can ask the container "did this host opt in to the proxy?".
    • Depends on: nothing.
    • Concept: a DI marker service: presence in the container is the signal, the instance carries no state.
    • Walkthrough: no members.
    • Why it's built this way: checking a private marker type is cheaper and more precise than probing for a public service a host could register for other reasons (for example the options type, which binding alone would create).
    • Where it's used: SameOriginApiProxyEndpointExtensions throws when it is absent, naming the missing call (SameOriginApiProxyEndpointExtensions.cs:38-42); ClientConfigEndpointExtensions reads it to decide whether to publish the proxy's path prefix to the client (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.cs:139,144).

    SameOriginApiProxySettings

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SameOriginApiProxySettings.cs:22 · Level 0 · class

    • What it is: the options class for the same-origin API proxy, bound from configuration section SameOriginApiProxy (SameOriginApiProxySettings.cs:25) and validated at startup.
    • Depends on: SameSiteMode (ASP.NET Core); first-party only by reference: the gateway address falls back to ApiSettings's ApiEndpoint.
    • Concept: options pattern with fail-fast validation, same shape as the other settings classes in this group (for example BlazorCspSettings with BlazorCspSettingsValidator). [Rubric §33, Developer Experience] assesses whether misconfiguration surfaces early and clearly; every knob here has a default, so a host opts in with no configuration at all.
    • Walkthrough:
      • DefaultTokenIssuingPaths = auth/login, auth/register, auth/oauth/exchange, auth/sign-in-link/redeem, auth/passkeys/signin (SameOriginApiProxySettings.cs:33): the endpoints whose successful response carries a token pair; sign-in links and passkey sign-in are included because script may not seed the cookies (:27-32).
      • PathPrefix = /api (:40): a request to {PathPrefix}/orders/5 is forwarded to {gateway}/orders/5.
      • GatewayAddress (:48): null by default; AddCommonSameOriginApiProxy fills it from Api:ApiEndpoint when unset (SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions.cs:57-64), so an Aspire discovery name such as https+http://gateway resolves as it does for the host's API clients.
      • AdditionalTokenIssuingPaths (:54): empty; a host adds paths such as auth/2fa/verify.
      • MaxRequestBodySizeByPath (:77): an empty, case-insensitive IDictionary<string, long> of per-endpoint request body caps in bytes that replace the server default (Kestrel's 30,000,000 bytes). Each key is a gateway-relative path shaped like RefreshPath (for example uploads/file); it covers that path and everything below it on a whole-segment boundary (uploads/file covers uploads/file/5, not uploads/files), the longest matching key wins, and every other path keeps the server default (:56-76). Without an entry, an upload over the default is refused 413 by this host before a byte reaches the gateway. A key containing / cannot be set from an environment variable, so use a JSON file or another provider that accepts arbitrary keys (:73-75). Enforced by SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint and checked by SameOriginApiProxySettingsValidator.
      • RefreshPath = auth/refresh (:84): answered by the proxy itself from the refresh cookie.
      • RevokePath = auth/revoke (:91): forwarded, then the cookies are cleared whatever upstream answered.
      • RevokeCurrentPath = auth/revoke/current (:99): the this-device sign-out the everyday Logout calls, treated exactly like RevokePath.
      • ViewAsEndPath = auth/view-as/end (:108, ADR-137): forwarded with the view-as overlay's bearer, then the overlay cookie is deleted whatever upstream answered. A POST to any path whose last segment is view-as is a view-as grant whose token goes into the overlay cookie and never reaches script (:101-107).
      • SessionCookieSameSite = SameSiteMode.Strict (:116); Lax is the only other accepted value.
    • Why it's built this way: recorded in ADR-131: a WebAssembly client calling the gateway cross-origin cannot carry the HttpOnly session cookie, so tokens end up script-readable; a same-origin proxy on the UI host lets the cookie authenticate data calls instead.
    • Where it's used: SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions (binding, and copying SessionCookieSameSite onto SessionCookieSettings, SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions.cs:69-74), SameOriginApiProxySettingsValidator, SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint, SameOriginApiProxyEndpointExtensions and ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.cs:144.

    SameOriginProxyInvoker

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SameOriginProxyInvoker.cs:19 · Level 0 · class

    • What it is: an IDisposable holder for the one HttpMessageInvoker YARP's forwarder sends every proxied request through (SameOriginProxyInvoker.cs:19,37).
    • Depends on: IServiceDiscoveryHttpMessageHandlerFactory (Microsoft.Extensions.ServiceDiscovery), SocketsHttpHandler, YARP's ReverseProxyPropagator.
    • Concept: YARP's IHttpForwarder expects a long-lived invoker with a transport tuned for proxying, not a pooled HttpClient. [Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability] assesses connection reuse and resource lifetime: one singleton transport is shared by all requests.
    • Walkthrough:
      • The public ctor resolves the optional discovery factory and builds the handler (SameOriginProxyInvoker.cs:24-31); the invoker is created with disposeHandler: false and the class keeps _ownedHandler to dispose itself (:22,39-43).
      • An internal ctor takes a test-supplied handler, for example a TestServer's (:34-35); that handler is not owned or disposed.
      • CreateHandler (:45-69) configures SocketsHttpHandler: UseProxy = false, AllowAutoRedirect = false, no automatic decompression, UseCookies = false, multiple HTTP/2 connections, ConnectTimeout 15 s, and a ReverseProxyPropagator over DistributedContextPropagator.Current (:50-59). When discovery is registered it wraps the transport (:61) so https+http://gateway resolves. The null-out-then-finally pattern disposes the transport only if wrapping throws.
    • Why it's built this way: redirects, cookies and decompression must pass through to the browser untouched, which is why they are all off; the propagator keeps the trace context flowing to the gateway.
    • Where it's used: injected into SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint (SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint.cs:31,427), registered by SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions.cs:78, and built from a handler in the test harness MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/SameOriginProxy/ProxyTestHarness.cs.

    • What it is: a private nested record (AccessToken, RefreshToken) of SessionHandoffProtector (SessionHandoffProtector.cs:75), the plaintext shape serialized to JSON before it is sealed.

    ViewAsOverlayTreatment

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SameOriginProxyTransformer.cs:38 · Level 0 · record struct

    • What it is: an internal readonly record struct describing what one forwarded request does with the view-as overlay cookie (ADR-137): OverlayPresent, ForwardsOverlayBearer, DeleteOverlay and the SameSite mode to write or delete the cookie with (SameOriginProxyTransformer.cs:37-38).
    • Depends on: SameSiteMode (ASP.NET Core); nothing first-party.
    • Concept: a per-request decision computed once by the endpoint and handed to the transformer, the same split as ProxyResponseMode. The overlay itself, a short-lived cookie holding a read-only view-as token, is ViewAsOverlayCookie.
    • Walkthrough:
      • Built by ResolveOverlay in SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint (SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint.cs:407-419): OverlayPresent when the cookie exists; ForwardsOverlayBearer when the overlay is live (unexpired) and the mode is neither TokenIssuing nor Revoke, in which case the overlay's token replaces the session bearer; DeleteOverlay when the cookie is present but no longer live; SameSite copied from SameOriginApiProxySettings.SessionCookieSameSite.
      • Read by SameOriginProxyTransformer in ShouldDeleteOverlay (SameOriginProxyTransformer.cs:162-167) and when writing or deleting the cookie (:103,210); default (all false) means "no overlay", which is the transformer's parameter default (:56).
      • ForwardsOverlayBearer also turns off the endpoint's 401 capture (SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint.cs:236-237), so a view-as bearer is never refreshed or replayed.
    • Why it's built this way: the endpoint owns cookie reading and the clock; the transformer stays free of both and only acts on four precomputed values.
    • Where it's used: SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint and SameOriginProxyTransformer only; it is internal.

    SameOriginApiProxySettingsValidator

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SameOriginApiProxySettingsValidator.cs:16 · Level 1 · class

    • What it is: the IValidateOptions<SameOriginApiProxySettings> that fails the boot on an unusable proxy configuration, collecting every failure into one result (SameOriginApiProxySettingsValidator.cs:16,21-69).
    • Depends on: SameOriginApiProxySettings; SearchValues<char>, ValidateOptionsResult.
    • Concept: startup validation via ValidateOnStart, cross-referenced to BlazorCspSettingsValidator. [Rubric §11, Security] applies to the SameSite check: only Strict or Lax pass, because the cookie now authenticates data calls (:42-45).
    • Walkthrough:
      • ForbiddenPathCharacters = {}*?#\ (:18): route syntax, query, fragment and backslash.
      • PathPrefix must pass IsValidPrefix (:28-33,71-77): non-blank, longer than one char, starts with /, does not end with /, no whitespace, no forbidden char. It becomes a route pattern, hence the literal-path rule.
      • GatewayAddress must be an absolute URI with a host (:35-40); the message names the Api:ApiEndpoint fallback.
      • RefreshPath, RevokePath, RevokeCurrentPath, ViewAsEndPath and every AdditionalTokenIssuingPaths entry must pass IsValidRelativePath (:47-51,79-84): not blank after trimming /, no whitespace, no forbidden char, no ://.
      • Every MaxRequestBodySizeByPath entry (:53-66): the key must pass the same IsValidRelativePath, and the limit must be positive (limit <= 0 fails), because a zero or negative cap would refuse every body on that path. Both failures are collected, not short-circuited.
    • Why it's built this way: an invalid prefix would otherwise surface as a route-pattern exception or a silently unmatched route at request time; naming the setting at boot is cheaper to diagnose.
    • Where it's used: registered with TryAddEnumerable by SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions.cs:66-67.

    SessionHandoffProtector

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SessionHandoffProtector.cs:16 · Level 1 · class

    • What it is: seals tokens with ASP.NET Core Data Protection so the Blazor Server circuit can pass them through browser script without script being able to read or replay them later (SessionHandoffProtector.cs:16).
    • Depends on: IDataProtectionProvider / ITimeLimitedDataProtector (Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection); nested TokenPair.
    • Concept introduced, the protected handoff. With the proxy enabled the HttpOnly cookies are the only session store, but a Server circuit runs over a WebSocket where it cannot read cookies on demand, and it may need to seed the cookies after a sign-in. The handoff hops through JS interop carrying an opaque blob that only this server can open, valid for one minute. [Rubric §26, Front-End Security] assesses keeping credentials out of script-reachable storage: the browser holds ciphertext with a 1-minute lifetime, never a usable bearer.
    • Walkthrough:
      • Lifetime = 1 minute, "one fetch plus one interop hop" (:19).
      • Two purpose-isolated protectors under the root MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy.SessionHandoff, one for AccessToken, one for TokenPair (:21-27), so a blob minted for one cannot be opened as the other.
      • ProtectAccessToken / UnprotectAccessToken (:29,31); ProtectTokenPair serializes a TokenPair to JSON (:33-34); UnprotectTokenPair returns a tuple or null on a missing, blank or malformed pair (:36-55).
      • TryUnprotect (:57-73) maps null or whitespace input, and CryptographicException or FormatException (tampered, expired, wrong purpose, retired key), to null.
    • Why it's built this way: see ADR-131. Returning null instead of throwing lets each endpoint answer a clean 401 or 400.
    • Where it's used: SessionHandoffEndpoints, HandoffTokenRefresher, HandoffSessionCookieSync; registered as a singleton at SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions.cs:80; tested in MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/SameOriginProxy/SameOriginApiProxyAuthFlowTests.cs and SessionHandoffServicesTests.cs.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: whether the host's Data Protection key ring is persisted and shared across replicas is host configuration; AddDataProtection() here (SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions.cs:77) adds no persistence. Not determinable from this source.

    • What it is: the proxy-mode ISessionCookieSync for the Blazor Server circuit: after a sign-in it hands the browser a protected token pair to post back, instead of the raw tokens (HandoffSessionServices.cs:52).

ClearAsync calls mmcaAuthCookie.clear (:53-63). Both return false when interop is unavailable (InvalidOperationException, JSDisconnectedException, JSException, OperationCanceledException, :65-66).

    HandoffTokenRefresher

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/HandoffSessionServices.cs:14 · Level 2 · class

    • What it is: the proxy-mode ISessionAwareTokenRefresher (an ITokenRefresher) for the Blazor Server circuit: it gets an access token from the cookie session through a protected handoff (HandoffSessionServices.cs:14).
    • Depends on: IJSRuntime, SessionHandoffProtector.
    • Concept: cross-reference SessionHandoffProtector; it replaces the default refresher (compare DirectApiTokenRefresher).
    • Walkthrough: AcquireAccessTokenAsync is a thin wrapper that returns the AccessToken of TryAcquireAccessTokenAsync (:16-17). The latter calls mmcaAuthHandoff.getToken (:24), whose script calls /auth/session/handoff and answers null only for the endpoint's 401. A null handoff yields TokenAcquisition.NoSession (:25-28). Otherwise the blob is unprotected server-side (:32): a non-empty token yields Acquired, while an empty result (expired handoff, or a key this host does not hold) yields Unavailable because it says nothing about the session itself (:32-34). Interop failure during SSR prerender, a disconnected circuit, a cancelled call or a transient endpoint failure also yields Unavailable (:36-42).

    SameOriginProxyTransformer

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SameOriginProxyTransformer.cs:50 · Level 4 · class

    • What it is: the per-request YARP HttpTransformer that rewrites the outbound request (path, bearer, cookies) and treats the response according to its ProxyResponseMode and its ViewAsOverlayTreatment (SameOriginProxyTransformer.cs:50-56).
    • Depends on: ISessionCookieStore, SessionCookieEndpoints (cookie names), ViewAsOverlayCookie, SessionClaimsToken, AuthClaimTypes, SameOriginProxyHeaders; YARP HttpTransformer and RequestUtilities, JwtSecurityTokenHandler.
    • Concept: [Rubric §26, Front-End Security] (credentials kept out of script): neither the token pair from a sign-in nor the token from a view-as grant reaches the browser body, and the cookie jar's token copies never reach the upstream.
    • Walkthrough:
      • TransformRequestAsync (:64-86): runs YARP's default, strips the prefix to build the destination URI (:72-75), sets Authorization: Bearer from the bearer it was given (the session's or the view-as overlay's) or removes it (:77), drops the CSRF header (:78), removes the session and overlay cookies (:79), and in TokenIssuing or ViewAsGrant mode clears Accept-Encoding so the body arrives as plain JSON (:81-85).
      • TransformResponseAsync (:88-125): when captureUnauthorized is on and upstream answered 401, sets UnauthorizedCaptured and copies nothing so the endpoint can replay (:93-97); deletes the overlay cookie when ShouldDeleteOverlay says so (:101-104); in Revoke clears the session cookies whatever upstream said (:106-111); in TokenIssuing on success hands off to CompleteTokenIssuingAsync (:113-116); in ViewAsGrant on success rewrites the body into the overlay (:118-122).
      • CompleteTokenIssuingAsync / IssuedSession (:133-155): only a 200 or 201 opened a session and has its body rewritten; any other success (a 202 for a registration that awaits confirmation) is copied through with no-store and no cookie written (:145-147).
      • ShouldDeleteOverlay (:162-167): only when an overlay is present, and then when the endpoint marked it expired, on ViewAsEnd or Revoke, on a sign-in that opened a session, or on an upstream 401 to the overlay's bearer. A view-as token is never refreshed or replayed.
      • RewriteViewAsResponseAsync / TryMoveViewAsTokenToOverlay (:175-213): writes the token to the overlay cookie with its JWT expiry (:210) and replaces accessToken with its claims-only form, leaving the session cookies alone so the staff user's own session survives the view. TryReadViewAsExpiry (:267-286) accepts only a readable JWT carrying both the view-as actor and grant claims; anything else passes through with no cookie written.
      • RewriteTokenResponseAsync / TryMoveTokensToCookies (:221-260): parses the JSON case-insensitively, writes both tokens to the cookie store (:256), replaces accessToken with its claims-only form and empties refreshToken (:257-258), and sets no-store (:228-232). A body without a token pair passes through unchanged.
      • RemoveSessionCookies (:297-315): filters only the access, refresh and overlay cookie pairs (:58-59) from the Cookie header; other cookies pass.
    • Why it's built this way: the browser-facing JSON keeps its shape, so a client written for the non-proxy mode still parses a well-formed response (:216-220).
    • Where it's used: created per request by SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint (SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint.cs:421-422).

    SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint.cs:29 · Level 5 · class

    • What it is: the request handler behind {PathPrefix}/{**path}: gates the request, resolves the session from the cookies, forwards to the gateway with a bearer, and refreshes and replays once on an unexpected 401 (SameOriginApiProxyEndpoint.cs:29-35,71-120); it also raises or lowers the request body cap per path from SameOriginApiProxySettings.MaxRequestBodySizeByPath before the forward (:90,373-390), and swaps in the view-as overlay's bearer while a read-only view-as session (ADR-137) is live (:99,407-419).
    • Depends on: YARP IHttpForwarder, SameOriginProxyInvoker, ICookieSessionRefresher with SessionRefreshOutcome / SessionRefreshStatus, ISessionCookieStore, ViewAsOverlayCookie, SameOriginApiProxySettings, SameOriginProxyTransformer, ViewAsOverlayTreatment, SessionClaimsToken.
    • Concept introduced, a Backend-for-Frontend proxy. The UI host forwards same-origin calls to the gateway, so the browser's cookie authenticates them and the bearer is attached server-side. [Rubric §26, Front-End Security] assesses CSRF and origin defenses: a same-origin gate and a CSRF header gate run before anything is forwarded. [Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity] assesses graceful degradation: an undecided refresh answers 503 with Retry-After and keeps the session.
    • Walkthrough:
      • Config: RequestConfig uses a 100 s activity timeout and HTTP/1.1 with RequestVersionOrLower (:46-51), which lets YARP turn an HTTP/2 WebSocket into an HTTP/1.1 upgrade; DefaultRetryAfter 5 s (:54); _tokenIssuingPaths merges the defaults and additions case-insensitively (:57-61); _bodySizeLimits holds the configured (PathString, long) caps ordered longest path first, so the most specific entry wins (:63-69); ViewAsGrantSegment = view-as names the last path segment of the view-as grant action (:40-41).
      • InvokeAsync (:71-120): disables status code pages so a proxied empty 401/404 is not replaced by an HTML page (:77-80); runs TryAnswerBeforeForwardingAsync; normalizes the gateway-relative path and calls ApplyBodySizeLimit (:87-90), safe because nothing above has read the body and the forward is the first read; resolves the mode, with null meaning RefreshLocallyAsync (:92-97); calls ResolveOverlay (:99), and only when the overlay's bearer is not forwarded, for non-sign-in requests that carry a session cookie, calls ValidateOrRefreshAsync and fails via FailRefreshAsync when no session results (:100-111); forwards with 401 capture decided by CapturesUnauthorized (:113-114); replays on capture (:116-119).
      • ResolveOverlay (:407-419): builds the ViewAsOverlayTreatment. A live overlay's token replaces the session bearer for every mode except TokenIssuing (anonymous) and Revoke (which signs the staff user's own session out); an expired overlay is marked for deletion and the session takes over.
      • CapturesUnauthorized (:236-237): only a session bearer on a replayable request earns one refresh-and-replay; a view-as bearer refused upstream is never refreshed or replayed (the transformer drops the overlay instead).
      • ApplyBodySizeLimit (:373-390): returns untouched when no limits are configured or IHttpMaxRequestBodySizeFeature is absent or read-only (the body has started being read); otherwise the first entry whose path covers the request on a whole segment, case-insensitively, sets MaxRequestBodySize. This is what stops an upload the API accepts being refused 413 by the UI host first.
      • Gates, in order (TryAnswerBeforeForwardingAsync, :252-281): CrossOriginRejection (403 cross_origin_rejected); OPTIONS answered 204 locally, never forwarded, so no preflight reaches the gateway and no CORS grant is made (:265-270); the other methods are forwarded with the browser's Origin intact because SameOriginProxyTransformer keeps YARP's default header copy, so the gateway's CORS middleware still sees them; unsafe methods other than an HTTP/2 WebSocket CONNECT need the CSRF header (403 csrf_header_required). HasCsrfHeader requires exactly one header value equal to SameOriginProxyHeaders's value (:125-128).
      • CrossOriginRejection (:146-152): OriginRejection refuses a foreign Origin and an upgrade with no Origin (:195-203); IsOwnOrigin compares scheme and server against the request as seen after forwarded headers, refusing paths, user info and the null origin (:161-175); FetchSiteRejection allows same-origin, and none only on a non-upgrade GET or HEAD (:205-222). IsWebSocketExtendedConnect detects RFC 8441 CONNECT (:184-187).
      • IsReplayable (:230-232): GET, HEAD or OPTIONS and not an upgrade, so nothing with a body is re-sent.
      • FailRefreshAsync (:296-307): Rejected ends the session (clear cookies, 401 session_expired, :284-288); anything else answers 503 session_refresh_unavailable with Retry-After from upstream or 5 s.
      • RefreshAndReplayAsync (:354-365): resets status to 200, forces RefreshAsync, forwards again without capture.
      • RefreshLocallyAsync (:441-476): under a live view-as overlay answers with the overlay's claims-only token and expiry and rotates nothing, since the overlay is never renewed (:443-458); otherwise rotates from the refresh cookie and answers the sign-in shape with a claims-only access token, empty refresh token and the expiry, no-store.
      • Four [LoggerMessage] warnings (:478-488); ForwardAsync logs a forward error only if the client did not abort (:424-434).
    • Why it's built this way: ADR-131 records the decision; the gateway stays the API edge and authorizes the forwarded bearer.
    • Where it's used: mapped by SameOriginApiProxyEndpointExtensions; its HasCsrfHeader is reused by SessionHandoffEndpoints (SessionHandoffEndpoints.cs:26,51); registered as a singleton at SameOriginApiProxyServiceExtensions.cs:79.

    SessionHandoffEndpoints

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.SameOriginProxy · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/SameOriginProxy/SessionHandoffEndpoints.cs:15 · Level 6 · class

    • What it is: maps the two Blazor Server circuit handoff endpoints, POST /auth/session/handoff and POST /auth/session-cookie/handoff (SessionHandoffEndpoints.cs:17-18,20).

    • Walkthrough:
      • Token handoff (:23-45): requires the CSRF header (else 403); while a live view-as overlay (ADR-137) is present, answers a HandoffBody with the overlay's protected token so the circuit holds what the page is viewing as, never refreshed (:31-36); otherwise calls GetOrRefreshAsync on the cookie session and answers 401 no_session or a HandoffBody with a protected access token. An expired overlay falls through to the session.
      • Cookie handoff (:48-67): requires the CSRF header, unprotects the token pair (400 invalid_handoff on failure), writes the cookies, answers 204.

    • Where it's used: called from MapCommonSameOriginApiProxy (SameOriginApiProxyEndpointExtensions.cs:54); reached from the browser by HandoffTokenRefresher and HandoffSessionCookieSync through their JS interop.

    ApiEndpointUrl

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Security · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Security/ApiEndpointUrl.cs:12 · Level 0 · class (internal, static)

    • What it is: the one shared test for whether a configured API endpoint value is usable, applied by the Content-Security-Policy provider, the /client-config endpoint and the Blazor Web host registration, so a deployment placeholder such as SET-VIA-ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLE is refused the same way everywhere instead of booting a client against a non-URL (class doc, ApiEndpointUrl.cs:5-11).
    • Depends on: nothing first-party. Externals: BCL Uri (Uri.TryCreate, Uri.UriSchemeHttp, Uri.UriSchemeHttps), System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis (NotNullWhenAttribute).
    • Concept introduced, one definition of "a usable endpoint" for every consumer of the same keys. The fail-fast configuration contract of ADR-070 asks that a misconfigured setting be caught at startup or at its first use, with one meaning. Three call sites read Api:ApiEndpoint and Api:WasmApiEndpoint; when each wrote its own check they could disagree about what a placeholder is. This class is the single answer, and it is strict about scheme: a value only qualifies when Uri.TryCreate(..., UriKind.Absolute, ...) succeeds AND the scheme is http or https (ApiEndpointUrl.cs:37-39), because on Linux a rooted path such as /relative/path parses as an absolute file:// URI (doc, lines 27-30).
      • [Rubric §26, Front-End Security] assesses browser-side hardening: the CSP's connect-src origin is derived from a value this class has already accepted, so a non-http(s) string never becomes a policy source.
    • Walkthrough
      • TryParseAbsoluteHttp(string? value, out Uri? uri) (lines 35-47) rejects null or whitespace, then requires an absolute parse with an http(s) scheme; on success it hands back the parsed Uri ([NotNullWhen(true)], line 35), otherwise uri is null.
      • IsAbsoluteHttp(string? value) (line 52) is the boolean form of the same test.
      • IsAbsoluteHttpOrServiceDiscovery(string? value) (lines 63-74) accepts everything IsAbsoluteHttp does, plus an Aspire service-discovery URL whose scheme is a +-joined list made only of http and https, such as https+http://gateway (lines 70-73). The doc (lines 54-60) scopes it: that form is valid only for the server head's Api:ApiEndpoint, which IHttpClientFactory clients resolve through the service-discovery handler AddServiceDefaults() adds; a browser cannot, so Api:WasmApiEndpoint uses IsAbsoluteHttp.
      • IsHttpScheme (lines 76-78) compares the scheme to Uri.UriSchemeHttp and Uri.UriSchemeHttps with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase.
    • Why it's built this way: a static, internal helper keeps the rule in one place without widening the package's public API, and splitting the browser form from the server form encodes the real difference (who can resolve a service-discovery name) instead of letting the looser test leak into the browser configuration.
    • Where it's used: BlazorCspPolicyProvider calls TryParseAbsoluteHttp to pin connect-src (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Security/BlazorCspPolicyProvider.cs:55); ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.MapClientConfigEndpoint throws when Api:WasmApiEndpoint fails IsAbsoluteHttp (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.cs:81-88); BlazorWebHostExtensions throws at registration when Api:ApiEndpoint fails IsAbsoluteHttpOrServiceDiscovery (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Hosting/BlazorWebHostExtensions.cs:114-121). Pinned by ApiEndpointUrlTests (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/Security/ApiEndpointUrlTests.cs).

    TrustedCallerHandler

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Security · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Security/TrustedCallerHandler.cs:35 · Level 0 · class (sealed, DelegatingHandler)

    • What it is: an outgoing HttpClient handler that stamps a shared-secret header onto a request only when the request targets the configured gateway origin, so the gateway can trust that the call came from this app rather than from an arbitrary caller.
    • Depends on: nothing first-party. Externals: System.Net.Http (DelegatingHandler, HttpRequestMessage, HttpResponseMessage), BCL Uri.
    • Concept introduced, an edge-trust header scoped to origin match, not applied blindly. [Rubric §11, Security] assesses whether a trust signal is bounded to the audience it is meant for. The constructor takes a header name, a shared secret, and the gateway origin (TrustedCallerHandler.cs:39), and SendAsync only stamps the header when the outgoing request's scheme, host, and port match that origin (TrustedCallerHandler.cs:57-63); a request to any other destination goes out unmodified, so the secret cannot leak to a third-party origin the same HttpClient happens to call. ADR-088 is the policy this enforces on the client side.
    • Walkthrough
      • The constructor (TrustedCallerHandler.cs:39-48) null/blank-guards headerName and secret and null-guards gatewayOrigin, storing all three as readonly fields.
      • SendAsync (TrustedCallerHandler.cs:51-72) null-guards the request, then compares request.RequestUri against _gatewayOrigin with Uri.Compare over UriComponents.Scheme | UriComponents.HostAndPort, case-insensitive (TrustedCallerHandler.cs:57-63). On a match it removes any existing value for the header and adds exactly one via TryAddWithoutValidation (TrustedCallerHandler.cs:67-68); the comment (TrustedCallerHandler.cs:65-66) explains the replace-not-append choice, the gateway compares one header value in constant time, so a second value would silently fail the comparison. It then calls base.SendAsync unconditionally.
    • Why it's built this way: a DelegatingHandler composes into the existing HttpClient pipeline without every call site having to remember to add the header itself, and gating on origin means the same registered handler is safe to reuse on a client that also talks to other hosts.
    • Where it's used: registered in MMCA.Common.UI.Web's DependencyInjection (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/DependencyInjection.cs); its behavior is pinned by TrustedCallerHandlerTests (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/Security/TrustedCallerHandlerTests.cs).

    • What it is: the bindable options type for an opt-in frame-src allowance on the Blazor host's Content-Security-Policy, one string list of origins a page may embed in an <iframe> (BlazorCspSettings.cs:23-35).

SectionName = "BlazorCsp" (line 28) names the configuration section; FrameSources (line 42) initializes to an empty list, so an unconfigured host emits no frame-src directive at all and the policy stays byte-identical to the pre-existing baseline (comment, lines 30-33). Only a deployment that needs to embed a specific third-party origin (the doc comment's example is a map provider's embed endpoint, lines 30-31) adds entries.
      • The doc comment (lines 33-40) states the origin shape a configured entry must satisfy: an absolute https origin with no path, query, fragment, user info, wildcard, quote, semicolon, comma or whitespace, so the field carries the contract BlazorCspSettingsValidator enforces rather than leaving it implicit.

    • Where it's used: bound and validated in MMCA.Common.UI.Web's DependencyInjection (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/DependencyInjection.cs), consumed by BlazorCspPolicyProvider's constructor as IOptions<BlazorCspSettings>.

    BrowserOriginHandler

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Services · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Services/BrowserOriginHandler.cs:32 · Level 0 · class (internal sealed, DelegatingHandler)

    • What it is: an outgoing HttpClient handler that stamps the visitor's browser origin (X-Forwarded-For with its address, User-Agent with its user-agent) on the server-side "APIClient" calls a Blazor Server host makes for that visitor (BrowserOriginHandler.cs:5-11). Without it the API would see this host's own address for every visitor, and the host's HTTP client sends no user-agent at all.
    • Depends on: nothing first-party. Externals: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http (IHttpContextAccessor, ConnectionInfo.RemoteIpAddress), System.Net.Http (DelegatingHandler, HttpRequestMessage).
    • Concept introduced, per-client policy keyed on the visitor rather than the host. [Rubric §11, Security] assesses whether a trust or rate-limit signal is attributed to the right principal. The API keys the registration rate limit, the session's recorded IP and the recorded device on the caller; behind a Blazor Server host every caller would collapse onto the host's address. The handler copies two values from the HTTP request that carries the work (the page request during prerender, the connection the circuit was established on afterwards, BrowserOriginHandler.cs:14-17). The address is RemoteIpAddress, which has already passed through this host's forwarded-headers middleware, so it is only as far back as the host trusts its own proxies, and a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For is never copied verbatim (BrowserOriginHandler.cs:16-19).
    • Walkthrough
      • The primary constructor (line 32) takes IHttpContextAccessor, an async-local that crosses the handler's own DI scope (parameter doc, lines 30-31). Two internal constants name the headers: ForwardedForHeaderName (line 35) and UserAgentHeaderName (line 38).
      • SendAsync (lines 41-55) null-guards the request, reads httpContextAccessor.HttpContext (line 47) and, only when a request is in scope, calls Replace for the connection's remote address (line 50) and the request's User-Agent (line 51), then calls base.SendAsync unconditionally (line 54). With no visitor behind the call (a background job) nothing is sent.
      • Replace (lines 57-68) returns early on a null or blank value (lines 59-62), so a blank user-agent is not forwarded; otherwise it removes any existing header (line 66) and adds exactly one value via TryAddWithoutValidation (line 67). The comment (lines 64-65) gives the reason for skipping validation: a real browser user-agent does not always parse as a strict product-token list, and neither value needs parsing on this side.
    • Why it's built this way: a DelegatingHandler composes into the named client's pipeline without any call site remembering to add the headers, and replace-not-append keeps each header single-valued so a caller cannot smuggle a second value in. It is the same shape as TrustedCallerHandler, but unconditional on origin because the target is always this app's own API.
    • Where it's used: registered transient and attached to the "APIClient" named client by AddCommonServerTokenStorage() in the MMCA.Common.UI.Web DependencyInjection (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/DependencyInjection.cs:47-48); only a Blazor Server host calls that, because the WebAssembly client reaches the API through the same-origin proxy, which forwards the browser's own headers (BrowserOriginHandler.cs:23-28). Pinned by BrowserOriginHandlerTests (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/Services/BrowserOriginHandlerTests.cs).

    BlazorCspSettingsValidator

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Security · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Security/BlazorCspSettingsValidator.cs:13 · Level 1 · class (internal, sealed)

    • What it is: the startup IValidateOptions<BlazorCspSettings> that rejects a frame-src origin the moment it is misshapen, so a bad entry fails fast rather than silently reaching the CSP header.
    • Depends on: first-party: BlazorCspSettings (the options type it validates). Externals: Microsoft.Extensions.Options (IValidateOptions<T>, ValidateOptionsResult), BCL SearchValues<char>, Uri.
    • Concept introduced, an explicit character denylist plus a shape check, not a regex. The fail-fast configuration contract of ADR-070 (Website/docs-src/adr/070-fail-fast-configuration-contract.md) assesses whether a misconfigured setting is caught at startup instead of at request time. Validate (lines 21-31) runs every configured FrameSources entry through IsValidOrigin and fails the whole registration with one message per bad entry (lines 26-30) rather than starting the host on a policy it cannot honor.
      • ForbiddenCharacters (line 18, a SearchValues<char> over *'";,@?#) is the set that could either break out of a CSP source expression or widen it, plus the URL delimiters (user info, query, fragment) a plain origin never carries. IsValidOrigin (lines 21-25 of the walkthrough below) rejects on that set before it ever calls Uri.TryCreate, so a value crafted to look like a URL but carrying a CSP metacharacter never reaches the parser.
      • [Rubric §26, Front-End Security] assesses browser-side hardening; this validator is what keeps BlazorCspSettings's contract (an absolute https origin, no path, wildcard, or delimiter) a checked invariant instead of a comment.
    • Walkthrough
      • Validate(string? name, BlazorCspSettings options) (lines 21-31) null-guards options, projects every entry that fails IsValidOrigin into a message naming the section, the entry, and the shape it must satisfy (lines 26-30), and returns ValidateOptionsResult.Success only when that list is empty.
      • IsValidOrigin(string? source) (lines 34-49), internal static: rejects null, whitespace-only, any entry containing whitespace, anything matching ForbiddenCharacters, or anything Uri.TryCreate cannot parse as absolute (lines 36-41). What remains must be https (ordinal case-insensitive), have a non-empty host, and have PathAndQuery equal to exactly "/" (lines 46-48); the comment (lines 44-45) notes the forbidden set already rules out user info, a query, and a fragment, so a root-only path is the last thing separating an origin from a full URL.
      • ToOrigin(string source) (lines 55-56), internal static: new Uri(source, UriKind.Absolute).GetLeftPart(UriPartial.Authority), the canonical scheme://host[:port] form used to splice a validated entry into the CSP header, lower-cased host, default port dropped, no trailing slash.
    • Why it's built this way: an explicit character denylist checked before parsing is stricter than trusting Uri alone, because Uri will happily parse strings a CSP source expression cannot safely contain; failing every bad entry at once (rather than the first) gives a deployment the whole list of what to fix in one pass.
    • Where it's used: registered alongside BlazorCspSettings in MMCA.Common.UI.Web's DependencyInjection (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/DependencyInjection.cs); ToOrigin is reused by BlazorCspPolicyProvider's BuildFrameSrc to canonicalize an already-validated entry.

Status-code-pages re-execution keeps the original status on the response, so a 403 re-executed to /not-found is still 403 while that page renders (lines 8-9).     BlazorCspPolicyProvider

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Security · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/Security/BlazorCspPolicyProvider.cs:28 · Level 2 · class (internal, sealed)

    • What it is: the Content-Security-Policy provider for a Blazor Web host. It computes one CSP string at construction, pinning connect-src to 'self' plus the configured API or Gateway origin (https and its matching WebSocket origin), optionally adding an opt-in frame-src directive, and hands the result to the shared security-headers middleware on every request.
    • Depends on: first-party: ICspPolicyProvider (the contract it implements, line 28), CspPolicy (the value it returns, a policy string plus an Enforce flag), SecurityHeadersMiddleware (its only consumer, named in the class doc at line 12), ApiSettings (the endpoint source, injected as IOptions<ApiSettings>, line 34), ApiEndpointUrl (the shared endpoint test, TryParseAbsoluteHttp, line 55), and BlazorCspSettings (the frame-src source, injected as IOptions<BlazorCspSettings>, line 35) whose entries it canonicalizes with BlazorCspSettingsValidator.ToOrigin (line 90). Externals: Microsoft.Extensions.Options (IOptions<T>), Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting (IWebHostEnvironment), Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http (HttpContext), BCL Uri.
    • Concept introduced, a computed CSP that fails closed. [Rubric §26, Front-End Security] assesses whether the browser is told which origins may load scripts and open connections. A static CSP cannot express "this deployment's API origin", because that origin is configuration, so the policy is built rather than hard-coded. The two directives that matter for exfiltration are locked: script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' (line 102, where the WASM allowance is what lets the Blazor WebAssembly runtime instantiate) and the computed connect-src (line 65). The load-bearing decision is what happens when the origin cannot be determined. The provider narrows connect-src to 'self', keeps the rest of the policy unchanged, and stays enforced (Enforce: true, line 59). A misconfigured endpoint therefore surfaces immediately as blocked API calls in the browser console rather than as a permissive header that protects nothing and that nobody notices, and the class doc states the reasoning outright: a security response header that quietly stops being enforced is the worse failure mode (lines 16-20).
      • [Rubric §11, Security] assesses the wider defense posture; this class is one control in a chain that also includes the session-cookie auth design and the security-headers middleware, and it is deliberately internal (line 28) so the only supported way to get it is the registration call, not a hand-wired new.
      • frame-src is opt-in and null-safe. BlazorCspSettings's default is an empty FrameSources list, and BuildFrameSrc (line 82) returns null when it is empty (lines 84-87), which keeps the policy byte-identical to the baseline for every deployment that has not opted in (comment, lines 79-81; class doc, lines 21-24).
    • Walkthrough
      • _policy (line 31) is a single CspPolicy field computed once. The constructor (lines 33-42) null-guards apiOptions, cspOptions, and environment and calls BuildCsp(apiOptions.Value, BuildFrameSrc(cspOptions.Value), environment.IsDevelopment()) (line 41). Because the type is registered as a singleton, this runs exactly once per process.
      • GetPolicy(HttpContext context) (line 45) ignores the context and returns the cached policy, so the per-request cost is a field read.
      • BuildCsp (lines 49-77) takes the pre-computed frameSrc as a parameter and resolves the endpoint as api.WasmApiEndpoint ?? api.ApiEndpoint (line 51). The guard on line 55 delegates to ApiEndpointUrl.TryParseAbsoluteHttp, the same test /client-config and AddMmcaBlazorWebHost apply to those keys (comment, lines 53-54): it rejects a blank value, a non-absolute URI, and any scheme that is not http or https, which matters on Linux, where a rooted path such as /relative/path parses as an absolute file:// URI. A rejected endpoint returns the enforced connect-src 'self' policy, still carrying frameSrc (line 59).
      • With a valid endpoint it derives origin via apiUri.GetLeftPart(UriPartial.Authority) (line 63, scheme://host:port), picks wss or ws to match (line 64), and composes connect-src 'self' {origin} {wsScheme}://{authority} (line 65). The WebSocket origin is there for the SignalR notification hub, so the live push channel is allowed without opening connect-src to the world.
      • Development only (lines 71-74) appends http://localhost:* and ws://localhost:* for Visual Studio Browser Link and Hot Reload, whose ports change per run (comment, lines 67-70); the production policy is untouched.
      • BuildFrameSrc(BlazorCspSettings settings) (lines 82-94) returns null on an empty FrameSources (lines 84-87), so the directive is omitted entirely rather than emitted empty; otherwise it maps every entry through BlazorCspSettingsValidator.ToOrigin, de-duplicates with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase (lines 89-91), and joins the result into "frame-src 'self' {origins}" (line 93). The comment (lines 79-81) notes every entry already passed the startup validator, so canonicalization here cannot fail.
      • BuildPolicy (lines 100-110) takes frameSrc as a parameter and assembles the directive list: default-src 'self', the script-src above plus 'unsafe-inline' in Development only (line 102, for the injected Hot Reload bootstrap), style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', img-src 'self' data: https: (line 104, deliberately open because profile pictures and content images come from arbitrary external hosts, per the comment on lines 96-99), font-src 'self', the computed connect-src, the frame-src directive when non-null (line 107, spliced in with its own trailing "; " so a null value leaves the rest of the policy unchanged), base-uri 'self', form-action 'self', and frame-ancestors 'none' (line 110, clickjacking protection).
    • Why it's built this way: computing once and caching keeps the hot path free, and returning a CspPolicy record rather than writing a header directly keeps the provider testable and lets one middleware own header emission. Registering it with AddSingleton (not TryAdd) is what makes it replace the default static provider, which is why the ordering rule in the class doc (lines 25-26) matters: call AddCommonBlazorCsp() before AddCommonSecurityHeaders. frame-src is threaded through as a plain string? parameter rather than read a second time inside BuildPolicy, so the policy string is built from one pass over its inputs. Delegating the endpoint test to ApiEndpointUrl means the CSP cannot accept a value the host registration or /client-config would refuse.
    • Where it's used: registered by AddCommonBlazorCsp() in the MMCA.Common.UI.Web DependencyInjection with AddSingleton<ICspPolicyProvider, BlazorCspPolicyProvider> (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/DependencyInjection.cs:67-77, whose XML doc, lines 53-58, describes the enforced connect-src 'self' fallback); the policy it returns is emitted by SecurityHeadersMiddleware. The class doc notes it was hoisted out of the app Blazor Web hosts where it had been byte-identical (line 25).
