    ClientConfigUiSections

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.ClientConfig · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigUiSections.cs:34 · Level 1 · class (internal static)

    • What it is: the helper that copies Common.UI's own Layout, Registration, SignIn and Legal settings from the server head's configuration into the anonymous /client-config document, so a value set where production values are set (an environment variable, Key Vault, appsettings.Production.json on the UI container) renders the same after WebAssembly hydration as in the prerender, with no second copy in the WebAssembly bundle (class summary, ClientConfigUiSections.cs:8-13).
    • Depends on: LayoutSettings, RegistrationSettings, SignInSettings and LegalSettings (each one's SectionName and type, ClientConfigUiSections.cs:39-42). Externals: Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration (IConfiguration, binder Get(Type)), System.Text.Json (JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase) and System.Reflection (PropertyInfo, BindingFlags).
    • Concept introduced, forward only what the settings class declares and what the server sets. [Rubric §26, Front-End Security] assesses what reaches the browser. The remarks (ClientConfigUiSections.cs:14-33) give two rules. Each section is bound to its Common.UI settings type and only that type's settable properties are written, so an unrelated or secret key that happens to sit under the same section name in the server configuration never reaches the anonymous document; every forwarded value is already rendered on public pages. And a section absent from the server configuration, or a property whose key is absent, is skipped, so the WebAssembly client's own defaults hold for everything the server leaves unset. [Rubric §20, Design System & Theming] applies because Layout (brand, footer) is one of the forwarded sections, so the theme a head configures survives hydration.
    • Walkthrough
      • Forwarded (ClientConfigUiSections.cs:37-43) is the fixed list of (SectionName, SettingsType) pairs, in the order they are written.
      • Build(IConfiguration) (ClientConfigUiSections.cs:51) loops the list (:53), skips a section that does not exist (:55-59) or binds to null (:61-65), then builds a dictionary keyed by the camelCased property name over the declared settable properties whose key is present in that section (section.GetSection(property.Name).Value is not null, :67-72), reading each value from the bound instance so the binder's type conversion applies. A section with no present key yields nothing; otherwise it yields the camelCased section name and the map (:74-77).
      • DeclaredSettableProperties(Type) (ClientConfigUiSections.cs:88-91) keeps public instance properties with a public setter or init accessor and no index parameters, which is what configuration binding writes; computed members such as LegalSettings.HasFooterLinks are excluded (doc :81-87). It is internal so the tests can reach it.
    • Why it's built this way: forwarding from the server's bound configuration means one place sets a production value; binding then reading back through the settings type keeps the document to the public shape the class declares. The host's extras win: a head that still adds one of these sections through its ClientConfig callback replaces the forwarded copy (remarks :28-32), because ClientConfigEndpointExtensions writes these sections before the extras.
    • Where it's used: called once per request by ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.MapClientConfigEndpoint (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.cs:104-107); pinned by ClientConfigEndpointTests (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointTests.cs).

    AuthenticatedServiceBase

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Api · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:17 · Level 2 · class (abstract)

    • What it is: the base class every UI-side HTTP service inherits. It supplies one shared Polly retry policy, two ways to get an HttpClient with a bearer token already attached, and the idempotency-key generator that makes those retries safe.
    • Depends on: ITokenStorageService, imported from the token namespace MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Auth.Tokens (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:5); its documentation also names AuthDelegatingHandler as the thing it deliberately bypasses and Auth.Tokens.ITokenRefresher, that is ITokenRefresher, as the source of the replay token. From MMCA.Common.Shared.Resilience (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:4) it reads RetryAfterHeader and the MaxRetryAfterWait ceiling on HttpResilienceDefaults. It also tests its storage for ISessionAwareTokenStorage (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:102), tells AuthDelegatingHandler which storage a bearer came from (AuthDelegatingHandler.TrackTokenOwner, AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:84), and reads the header name from IdempotencyHeaders (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:200). Externals: IHttpClientFactory, TimeProvider, Polly and Polly.Retry.
    • Concept introduced, why a base class and not just the handler pipeline. [Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity] assesses whether transient failures are absorbed rather than surfaced; the retry policy is that. The sharper teaching is in the CreateAuthenticatedClientAsync doc comment (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:63-68): IHttpClientFactory creates its handlers in a separate DI scope from the Blazor circuit, so a DelegatingHandler cannot reach the circuit's IJSRuntime to read the in-memory access token. The base class works around that by reading the token from the circuit-scoped storage service itself and setting the header directly. [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] covers the idempotency half: retrying a POST is only safe if the server can recognize the repeat, which is what ADR-017 provides.
    • Walkthrough
      • RetryPolicy is a protected static readonly AsyncRetryPolicy<HttpResponseMessage> built once from the shipped backoff (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:37), so one policy instance serves the whole app rather than one per service instance per circuit. ApiClientName pins the named client to "APIClient" (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:39), and both constructor arguments are null-checked into private fields (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:41-42).
      • SharedRetryPolicy (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:48) is an internal static getter that returns that same RetryPolicy instance. Its doc comment (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:44-47) names the only reader, IdempotentReadRetry, which reuses the exact policy object without inheriting from this class, so the anonymous read path and the authenticated one cannot drift apart.
      • NewIdempotencyKey() (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:61) returns a compact Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N"), and its remarks (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:53-59) carry the load-bearing rule: the value is generated once per logical operation and reused across every retry attempt, because the server-side idempotency filter keys its cached response off it. Generating a new key per attempt would defeat the dedup entirely and let a retry create a duplicate record.
      • CreateAuthenticatedClientAsync() (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:69) resolves the "APIClient" (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:71), reads the token (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:75), sets Authorization: Bearer when non-blank (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:76-85), and catches InvalidOperationException to proceed without a token during SSR prerender, when JS interop is unavailable (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:87-90). When it attaches a bearer it also calls AuthDelegatingHandler.TrackTokenOwner(token, _tokenStorageService) (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:84): the handler in the client's pipeline holds a different storage instance (its own DI scope), so it is told which instance the bearer came from, and a 401 to it reaches the storage the component's auth state listens to (comment, :81-83).
      • StorageRenewsRejectedTokens (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:102) is a private protected flag that is true when the storage is an ISessionAwareTokenStorage. Its doc comment (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:95-101) states the contract: such storage has already had the ONE renewal a 401 earns made on it by AuthDelegatingHandler before the 401 reaches the caller, so a caller replaying the request reads the renewed token instead of refreshing a second time. ReadRenewedAccessTokenAsync(string? rejectedToken) (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:113) is that read: it returns null when no bearer was sent (:115-118), and otherwise re-reads storage (:120) and returns the value only when it is non-blank and differs ordinally from the refused token (:121-123), so a session the renewal ended, or a storage still holding the refused token, yields nothing to replay with.
      • CreateClientWithToken(string accessToken) (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:134) is the replay path. Its doc comment (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:126-132) explains why it exists: after the API answers 401, the stored token still looks fresh by the client clock, so re-reading storage would just resend the token the server has already rejected. The caller passes the token it acquired straight from ITokenRefresher; the method rejects a blank one (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:136) and stamps the header unconditionally (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:139).
      • IsRetryableResponse(HttpResponseMessage, TimeProvider) (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:157) is the retry predicate. It first excludes 501 Not Implemented and 505 HTTP Version Not Supported (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:159-162) because, as the remarks say (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:148-156), those are permanent verdicts and retrying only burns the budget and delays the error the caller needs to see. It next refuses any response for which RetryAfterHeader.ExceedsRetryBudget is true (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:164-167; MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Resilience/RetryAfterHeader.cs:75): a 429 whose Retry-After asks for longer than HttpResilienceDefaults.MaxRetryAfterWait, 8 seconds (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Resilience/HttpResilienceDefaults.cs:40), means the rate-limit window will not reset within any wait worth holding the user for, so the refusal surfaces at once. It then asks IsReplaySafe whether the request may be sent again and gives up if not (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:169-172). Only then does it accept anything >= 500 plus 408 Request Timeout and 429 Too Many Requests (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:174-175), the two codes where the server is explicitly inviting a later attempt.
      • IsReplaySafe(HttpRequestMessage? request) (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:188) is the gate that keeps a retry from duplicating a write. Its doc comment (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:178-185) states the rule: GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE and the other idempotent verbs are always safe to re-send, while a POST or PATCH is safe only when it carries a non-blank Idempotency-Key header, which an [Idempotent] endpoint deduplicates on. Without a key, a failed attempt may still have run server-side, and a retry can hit a rate limit and replace the server's real failure with a 429. A response with no request attached is treated as safe (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:190-193). The method is internal static so a test can pin it directly, and the doc comment on RetryPolicy (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:21-36) carries the same POST/PATCH caveat.
      • The exception arm of the policy sees no response, so it learns replay safety another way. MarkReplaySafety(HttpRequestException, HttpRequestMessage) (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:221) stores IsReplaySafe(request) in exception.Data under the internal const ReplaySafeDataKey (:210); AuthDelegatingHandler, the outermost handler AddUIShared adds to the API client, calls it (doc comment :212-220, which notes that on a host calling AddServiceDefaults the service-discovery handler wraps it, and so does the standard resilience handler unless the host removes it, as AddMmcaBlazorWebHost does). IsRetryableException (:232) then retries a transport failure unless it was marked not replay-safe (a POST or PATCH without an Idempotency-Key) AND failed after the request may have been sent: only NameResolutionError, ConnectionError and SecureConnectionError (failures before send, the rule the gRPC client applies) still retry (:233-236, doc :224-231). An unmarked exception keeps the retry (Data[...] is not false, :233).
      • DefaultBackoff(int attempt) (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:246-248) is the shipped schedule: 500 * 2^(attempt - 1) milliseconds (0.5s, 1s, 2s for retries 1, 2 and 3) plus up to 250 ms of random jitter, so a fleet of clients does not re-converge on the same instant. It is internal so a test can pin the schedule (doc :240-245). The RetryPolicy doc comment (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:21-36) explains why the schedule is short: a read that fails fast spends at most about 4.25 seconds waiting between attempts before it surfaces, a backend that accepts the request and then hangs is cut off by the client's own timeout instead (HttpResilienceDefaults.TotalRequestTimeout, which the comment gives as 90 seconds, set where the API client is registered) and that cancellation is not retried, and a 429 that names a Retry-After is outside the 4.25-second bound because each such retry can wait up to the cap. The CA5394 suppression around it (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:238) documents that the randomness only spaces retries and feeds no security decision.
      • RetryDelay(int attempt, HttpResponseMessage? response, Func<int, TimeSpan> backoff, TimeProvider timeProvider) (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:261-269, doc :202-211) picks the wait before each retry. For a 429 Too Many Requests whose Retry-After parses through RetryAfterHeader.TryGetDelay (MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Shared/Resilience/RetryAfterHeader.cs:43) it waits exactly the named delay; everything else, including a 5xx and a transport failure with no response, keeps the backoff. The predicate has already refused a 429 over MaxRetryAfterWait, so the delay used here is bounded. The TimeProvider is the clock a date-form Retry-After is measured against.
      • BuildRetryPolicy(Func<int, TimeSpan> backoff, TimeProvider? timeProvider = null) (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:288-304) is internal and backoff- and clock-injectable so a test can exercise the disposal and Retry-After contracts without waiting out the real delays; a null clock falls back to TimeProvider.System (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:292). It retries 3 times (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:296-297), with sleepDurationProvider routed through RetryDelay (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:298). Its onRetryAsync disposes the retried attempt's response (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:299-303); the remarks (AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:275-282) explain that Polly hands the caller only the final outcome (the policy handles HttpRequestException through IsRetryableException, :294, and responses through IsRetryableResponse, :295), so without this every intermediate 5xx, 408 or 429 response leaks its content buffer and keeps its connection out of the handler pool until finalization, exactly under the sustained backend failure the retries exist to survive. A retried HttpRequestException carries no result, hence the null-conditional, and the final response is not disposed here because the caller owns it.
    • Why it's built this way: the DI scope mismatch is a real Blazor Server constraint, not a preference, so the workaround has to live somewhere every service shares. The retry ceiling and jitter line up with the resilience posture in ADR-009.
    • Where it's used: inherited by EntityServiceBase<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType> (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/EntityServiceBase.cs:38), ChildEntityServiceBase (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/ChildEntityServiceBase.cs:21), AuditHistoryService (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auditing/AuditHistoryService.cs:24) and NotificationInboxService (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Notifications/NotificationInboxService.cs:34), and through them by every module-level UI service in the consumer apps. The members show up as NewIdempotencyKey() on creates and updates (EntityServiceBase.cs:158 and EntityServiceBase.cs:182), RetryPolicy.ExecuteAsync around each call (EntityServiceBase.cs:285 and EntityServiceBase.cs:313) and CreateClientWithToken on the 401 replay (NotificationInboxService.cs:154). The policy itself is also reached without inheritance by IdempotentReadRetry (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/IdempotentReadRetry.cs:24), which gives anonymous lookup services the same retries on GETs.

    ClientConfigBuilder

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.ClientConfig · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigBuilder.cs:19 · Level 2 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the accumulator a host's own extras delegate writes into when it wants extra data served on the anonymous /client-config document, one named section per Add call.
    • Depends on: ClientConfigEndpointExtensions (its ApiSectionName and ModulesSectionName constants, checked as the two reserved names, ClientConfigBuilder.cs:51-52); Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http (HttpContext, BCL) and Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection / Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration for the two convenience accessors it republishes.
    • Concept, a builder with an internal constructor. [Rubric §26, Front-End Security] covers what this type prevents: the constructor is internal (line 23), so the only place a ClientConfigBuilder can come into existence is inside MapClientConfigEndpoint's own request delegate, which is also the one place a host's extras callback runs. A host cannot construct one ahead of time and stash arbitrary state in it outside the request it belongs to.
    • Walkthrough
      • _sections (line 21) is a Dictionary<string, object?> keyed with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase (a collection expression with with(...)), so "OAuth" and "oauth" collide as the same section.
      • HttpContext (line 26) and the two accessors built on it, Services (line 29, reads HttpContext.RequestServices) and Configuration (line 32, resolves IConfiguration from those services), let an extras delegate reach DI and configuration without the endpoint having to pass them separately.
      • Add(string name, object? value) (line 47) blank-checks name (ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace, line 49), rejects the reserved framework sections ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.ApiSectionName and ModulesSectionName case-insensitively, with a message naming the offending section (lines 51-57), then adds through _sections.TryAdd (line 59) so a second call with the same name throws rather than silently overwriting the first (lines 59-62). It returns this for chaining (line 64). The Common.UI settings sections (Layout, Registration, SignIn, Legal) are not reserved: adding one replaces the copy ClientConfigUiSections forwarded.
      • Sections (line 34) is internal, an IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?> view the endpoint reads back after the delegate returns; nothing outside this package can enumerate a builder's contents.
    • Why it's built this way: the reserved-name and duplicate-name guards live on the builder rather than being left to the endpoint's own loop, so every caller of Add, present or future, gets the same two checks for free. The internal constructor and internal Sections getter keep the type's read side as narrow as its write side: a host can only add, never inspect what a different extras call already added.
    • Where it's used: constructed once per request inside ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.MapClientConfigEndpoint's handler and handed to the caller's extras delegate (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.cs:90-91); its Sections are then read back to assemble the response document (ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.cs:109-112). Exercised directly by ClientConfigEndpointTests (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointTests.cs).

    ClientConfigEndpointExtensions

    MMCA.Common.UI.Web · MMCA.Common.UI.Web.ClientConfig · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointExtensions.cs:19 · Level 2 · class (static)

    • What it is: the extension that maps GET /client-config, the anonymous document a WASM client's bootstrap fetches to learn the browser-reachable API base address before it can hold a session, plus whatever extra sections the host contributes.
    • Depends on: ClientConfigBuilder (constructed per request, line 90), ApiSettings (IOptions<ApiSettings>, read for WasmApiEndpoint, line 80), ApiEndpointUrl (IsAbsoluteHttp, line 81), UIModuleConfiguration (IsModuleEnabled, line 127), ClientConfigUiSections (Build, line 104), and, only in a host running the same-origin API proxy, SameOriginApiProxyMarker (probed from request services, line 139) and SameOriginApiProxySettings (read for PathPrefix, line 144); externals Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing (IEndpointRouteBuilder, RouteHandlerBuilder), Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http (HttpContext), IConfiguration, System.Text.Json (JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase), and the ASP.NET Core minimal-API Results type.
    • Concept introduced, fail-closed instead of falling back. [Rubric §13, Observability & Operability] assesses whether a misconfigured host fails loudly and diagnosably rather than silently degrading. The endpoint's remarks (lines 41-49) state the rule directly: it serves Api:WasmApiEndpoint, the browser-reachable gateway URL, and never falls back to Api:ApiEndpoint, the server head's own service-discovery name, because a browser cannot resolve that name and serving it would hand the client a silently broken base address. A host whose value is missing, or is not an absolute http(s) URL (a deployment placeholder, for one), answers every request with a server error naming the key and the expected shape (lines 81-88), which surfaces as a failed client start instead of a client quietly pointed at the wrong API. This is the client-config instance of ADR-070.
    • Concept introduced, anonymous by declared necessity. [Rubric §11, Security] covers why this endpoint is one of the few that must allow anonymous access on purpose: the WASM client fetches this document before it can hold a session (remarks, lines 66-71), and a host's fallback authorization policy would otherwise gate it like any other endpoint that states nothing. The endpoint therefore declares AllowAnonymous() itself (line 116) rather than relying on an ambient default, and the remarks warn that only values the public site renders anyway belong in extras (lines 69-70).
    • Concept introduced, the head's module switches and UI settings travel with the document. [Rubric §18, UI Architecture] assesses how the render modes of one app stay consistent. The modules section lists every entry of the head's Modules configuration with ONLY its resolved enabled flag, never its other settings, so a module the head disables does not come back after the WebAssembly client hydrates (remarks, lines 50-57; see ADR-059). The layout, registration, signIn and legal sections carry the head's Common.UI settings, limited to declared properties and keys the server sets (remarks, lines 58-65), through ClientConfigUiSections.
    • Concept introduced, an additive key for the same-origin proxy. A host that runs the same-origin API proxy (ADR-131) gets one extra member in the Api section, sameOriginApiEndpoint, the proxy's origin-relative base (for example /api/) that the WASM bootstrap resolves against the page's own origin, while apiEndpoint stays the gateway for full-page navigations (doc, lines 130-136). The proxy's presence is detected from DI (the marker service), not from configuration, so every host without the proxy serves the section exactly as before and an existing client sees no change.
    • Walkthrough
      • Three public constants: ClientConfigPath = "/client-config" (line 22), ApiSectionName = "Api" (line 25) and ModulesSectionName = "Modules" (line 31), the two section names ClientConfigBuilder treats as reserved.
      • The extension(IEndpointRouteBuilder endpoints) block (line 33, see primer) holds the single member MapClientConfigEndpoint(Action<ClientConfigBuilder>? extras = null) (line 77).
      • The handler (lines 78-115) takes the request's HttpContext plus IOptions<ApiSettings>, reads apiSettings.Value.WasmApiEndpoint (line 80), throws InvalidOperationException naming the key when ApiEndpointUrl.IsAbsoluteHttp rejects it (lines 81-88), builds a ClientConfigBuilder for the request and invokes extras on it (lines 90-91), and seeds the response with the camelCased Api section from BuildApiSection(context, wasmApiEndpoint) and the camelCased Modules section from BuildModulesSection(builder.Configuration) (lines 95-99). It then writes the forwarded Common.UI sections from ClientConfigUiSections (lines 104-107) BEFORE the host's extras, so a head that still adds one of them replaces the forwarded copy rather than colliding with it (comment, lines 101-103), and finally overlays every builder section, each name run through the same JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase policy the web JSON defaults apply to members (lines 109-112), so the document's shape matches what an anonymous-object payload would have produced anyway.
      • The route is finished with .AllowAnonymous().ExcludeFromDescription() (lines 116-117): anonymous for the reason above, and excluded from the OpenAPI description because it is not a data endpoint a client integrates against, it is bootstrap plumbing.
      • The private BuildModulesSection(IConfiguration) (lines 124-128) maps each child of the Modules section, keyed as spelled there (case-insensitive dictionary), to new { Enabled = UIModuleConfiguration.IsModuleEnabled(configuration, module.Key) }; a head with no Modules section serves an empty object.
      • The private BuildApiSection(HttpContext, string) (lines 137-146) returns new { ApiEndpoint } when GetService<SameOriginApiProxyMarker>() is null (lines 139-142); otherwise it reads IOptions<SameOriginApiProxySettings>.Value.PathPrefix (line 144) and returns new { ApiEndpoint, SameOriginApiEndpoint = prefix + "/" } (line 145).
    • Why it's built this way: putting the base-address selection, the reserved-name policy and the camelCase conversion all in one mapped endpoint means every host that calls MapClientConfigEndpoint gets the identical fail-closed contract; a host only supplies the pieces specific to it through extras. The same-origin key is decided here too, from the proxy's own DI marker, so a host that adds the proxy does not have to remember a second client-config change.
    • Where it's used: called from a host's endpoint mapping alongside the other framework endpoints; its handler constructs ClientConfigBuilder (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web/ClientConfig/ClientConfigBuilder.cs, 3 call sites) and is pinned by ClientConfigEndpointTests (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Web.Tests/ClientConfig/ClientConfigEndpointTests.cs, 2 call sites).

    AuditHistoryPanel

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Components.Auditing · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Auditing/AuditHistoryPanel.razor.cs:22 · Level 3 · class (partial component, IDisposable)

    • What it is: the opt-in "who changed what, and when" panel of a detail page. It renders an entity's recorded changes (ADR-075) as one table row per change, with when, who, operation, field, the value before and the value after (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Components/Auditing/AuditHistoryPanel.razor:13-30), newest first, paged by a "Load more" button while a page comes back full.
    • Depends on: AuditHistoryEntryDTO (the row type, AuditHistoryPanel.razor.cs:24), Result<T> (the fetch delegate's return), and SharedResource through IStringLocalizer (line 34) for every heading, column, operation name and the "System" label. The markup reuses the framework's ListNoRecordsContent (retry on failure) and EmptyState (empty history) components (AuditHistoryPanel.razor:39,43). Externals: MudBlazor (MudPaper, MudSimpleTable, MudProgressLinear, MudButton).
    • Concept introduced, a fetch-delegate panel that owns its own paging and cancellation. [Rubric §18, UI Architecture] assesses whether components stay presentational and receive data through clear contracts. The panel never knows a URL or a service: it takes a FetchPage delegate (page number, page size, token in; a Result of entries out, line 42), so the page that hosts it decides where the history comes from. [Rubric §19, State Management & Data Flow] assesses how async state survives overlapping requests. A generation counter plus a per-fetch CancellationTokenSource means a superseded or disposed fetch can never write rows into the panel.
    • Walkthrough:
      • Parameters: FetchPage is [EditorRequired] (lines 40-42), PageSize defaults to 20 (line 45), Title falls back to the shared AuditHistory.Title text (line 48; markup line 6), and UserLabel, PropertyLabel and DisplayTimeZone (lines 51-57) map a user id, a property name and the display zone, each falling back to the raw value or UTC when null.
      • OnParametersSet throws InvalidOperationException when no FetchPage was supplied (lines 100-106). OnInitializedAsync loads page 1 only when RendererInfo.IsInteractive (line 110), so nothing is fetched during prerender.
      • LoadPageAsync (line 117) bumps _generation first (line 126), swaps in a fresh token source and cancels the previous one (line 133), then calls FetchPage(page, PageSize, token) (line 147). A result whose generation is stale is dropped; a failure records _failedPage (line 153 onward), which the markup turns into a retry; a success appends rows, sets _hasMore when the page came back full (line 161) and _firstPageEmpty for an empty page 1 (line 162). A cancellation caused by its own token is swallowed (line 164).
      • LoadMoreAsync asks for the next page (line 113), RetryAsync re-fetches the failed page (line 115), and the public ReloadAsync (line 64) clears every row and state flag and fetches page 1 again.
      • Formatting helpers: WhenText converts ChangedOn from UTC into DisplayTimeZone and appends the zone name (line 181), WhoText shows AuditHistory.System for a change with no user (lines 188-192), and FieldText blanks a row with no property name (line 198).
      • Dispose(bool) cancels and disposes the in-flight token source (lines 83-96).
    • Why it's built this way: the audit trail is opt-in per app (ADR-075, Website/docs-src/adr/075-audit-trail.md), so the panel is a plain component a detail page places inside its own AuthorizeView on the app's audit permission (class docs, lines 10-15), and the delegate keeps it independent of which host route serves the history.
    • Where it's used: fed by IAuditHistoryUIService on ADC's EventDetail and SessionDetail pages (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Events/EventDetail.razor.cs:42-45). Pinned by AuditHistoryPanelTests.

    IdempotentReadRetry

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Api · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/IdempotentReadRetry.cs:18 · Level 2 · class (static)

    • What it is: the retry that AuthenticatedServiceBase applies, made reachable without inheriting from it, so a service that makes anonymous reads (a lookup service that creates a plain APIClient) gets three retries instead of a single attempt (class summary, lines 5-8).
    • Depends on: AuthenticatedServiceBase for the policy instance, read through its internal SharedRetryPolicy (line 24, MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/AuthenticatedServiceBase.cs:48). Externals: Polly.Retry (AsyncRetryPolicy<HttpResponseMessage>, line 1) and BCL HttpClient.
    • Concept introduced, retry is only safe for an idempotent verb. [Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity] assesses whether transient failures are absorbed rather than surfaced on every call path, not just the inherited one. [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] covers the limit: the class remarks (lines 9-16) state that the policy re-sends on an HttpRequestException, a 5xx other than 501/505, 408 or 429, up to three times with 2s, 4s, 8s backoff plus jitter, and that re-sending is only safe when doing the operation twice is the same as doing it once. That is why the only entry point is a GET; a write that needs retries goes through EntityServiceBase<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType>, whose creates carry an Idempotency-Key the server deduplicates on.
    • Walkthrough
      • Policy (line 24) is an internal static getter returning AuthenticatedServiceBase.SharedRetryPolicy. Its doc comment (lines 20-23) stresses that it is the same object, not a copy built from the same settings, so the two paths cannot drift.
      • GetAsync(HttpClient httpClient, Uri requestUri, CancellationToken cancellationToken) (line 35) null-guards both arguments (lines 40-41) and returns Policy.ExecuteAsync(token => httpClient.GetAsync(requestUri, token), cancellationToken) (line 43), so the token is honored between attempts and by each send. The doc comment (lines 26-34) sets the ownership rule: every retried response is disposed by the policy, the caller owns and disposes the final one, and HttpRequestException escapes only when every attempt failed without a response.
    • Why it's built this way: sharing the instance rather than re-declaring the policy keeps one definition of "retryable" and one backoff schedule for the whole UI layer, including the response-disposal behavior of AuthenticatedServiceBase.BuildRetryPolicy. Exposing a GET-only surface instead of a general ExecuteAsync is the guardrail: the type cannot be used to retry a non-idempotent write by accident.
    • Where it's used: ADC lookup services that read anonymously, for example SpeakerLookupService (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Services/Speakers/SpeakerLookupService.cs:96), EventLookupService (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Services/Events/EventLookupService.cs:102), CategoryItemLookupService (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Services/Categories/CategoryItemLookupService.cs:54), SessionLookupService (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Lookups/SessionLookupService.cs:27,58) and NowNextService (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/HappeningNow/NowNextService.cs:26). Several of them pass it as the per-page fetch inside PagedReadAll. Pinned by IdempotentReadRetryTests (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/Api/IdempotentReadRetryTests.cs).

    HttpResultExecutor

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Api · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/HttpResultExecutor.cs:35 · Level 3 · class (static)

    • What it is: the wrapper every UI service call runs inside. It converts the faults that survive after a response has been handled, a refused connection, a DNS failure, a broken stream, a client timeout, into failed Result values, so a service method typed as returning a Result really does return one.
    • Depends on: Result and its generic sibling Result<T>, plus Error for the failure it mints (HttpResultExecutor.cs:2,133,136); System.Text.Json and System.Net.Http (BCL) plus Polly (HttpResultExecutor.cs:3) for the fault set it recognizes. It is static and holds no state, so anything can call it, including services that derive from none of this package's bases.
    • Concept introduced, the two halves of "a client call never throws". [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] assesses whether the error channel between client and server is explicit and typed. The framework's answer has two pieces and this is the second one. The first, ProblemDetailsResultReader, converts a response: it reads the server's ProblemDetails body back into errors with the original ErrorType intact. This class converts the absence of a response, and the class comment states the split outright (lines 12-17). Only with both does a page get to branch on a Result instead of writing a catch, which is what ADR-013 asks for (Website/docs-src/adr/013-result-pattern.md) and what ADR-094 records as the client contract (Website/docs-src/adr/094-client-entity-data-access.md:82-94). [Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity] applies because this is the boundary where an infrastructure fault stops being an exception and becomes something the UI can render.
    • Concept introduced, cancellation is not a failure. [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety] assesses whether the user-facing outcome of an interaction is honest. A page cancels its own work all the time: a disposed component, a grid fetch superseded by the next keystroke. Reporting that back as an error would paint a message for something the user never did. The class therefore distinguishes two identically typed exceptions by inspecting the token, and documents the rule on itself (lines 18-24).
    • Walkthrough
      • Two public constants name the failures it can mint, TransportErrorCode = "Http.TransportFailure" (line 38) and TimeoutErrorCode = "Http.Timeout" (line 41). They are public because they are the branch a page uses when it needs different wording; the two English messages are internal constants (lines 43-47), internal rather than private so that ResultUiExtensions can recognize the executor's own sentence (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Common/ResultUiExtensions.cs:366-371).
      • ExecuteAsync(Func<Task<Result>>, CancellationToken) (line 56) and its generic twin ExecuteAsync<T>(Func<Task<Result<T>>>, CancellationToken) (line 91) are the whole public surface. Both are structurally identical, and both start with ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull (lines 58,
        1. and cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested() (lines 63, 98). The pre-check is explained in the source (lines 60-62): an already-abandoned call must never reach the network, and the propagation contract has to hold even for an operation that would complete without ever observing the token.
      • The try simply awaits the caller's operation (lines 67, 102). Everything interesting is in the three catch clauses, and their order is the design.
      • catch (OperationCanceledException) when (cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) rethrows (lines 69-72, 104-107). This filter is the entire mechanism: the caller's token being cancelled is what identifies the exception as the caller's own.
      • The unfiltered catch (OperationCanceledException) (lines 73, 108) is therefore the other case: HttpClient gave up on its own timeout, which raises the same exception type with the token not cancelled. That one becomes a failure carrying TimeoutError() (lines 75, 110).
      • catch (Exception exception) when (IsTransportFault(exception)) (lines 77, 112) filters rather than catching broadly, so nothing outside the recognized set is swallowed. IsTransportFault (line 127) admits four types: HttpRequestException, IOException, JsonException and Polly's ExecutionRejectedException (line 128), the base of TimeoutRejectedException and BrokenCircuitException, so a client resilience pipeline that refuses to run or finish the call also becomes a failure (HttpResultExecutor.cs:3 imports Polly). The comment above it draws the line explicitly (lines 118-126): anything else is a programming fault and keeps travelling as an exception.
      • TransportError (line 130) puts the exception's own text on the error's Source rather than its Message (lines 131-133), because that text is diagnostic detail: not localizable, and not safe to render verbatim. TimeoutError (line 135) carries no detail at all.
    • Why it's built this way: the class comment records the third consequence of the split (lines 25-33): a transport failure never reached a server, so nothing localized it on the way back, which is why the two messages are English literals and why the codes are public. A page that needs translated wording does not read the synthesized message: ResultUiExtensions.LocalizedErrorMessage translates these two by their code, first through the localizer the page passes and then, when that has no such key, through the framework's own SharedResource pair for the current UI culture, and a page can also branch on the code or override the translation with the same key in its own resource pair. Keeping the type static and dependency-free is what lets services outside this package's hierarchy, including a consumer app's hand-written client, adopt the same contract with one call.
    • Where it's used: it wraps every dispatch in this package, EntityServiceBase<TEntityDTO, TIdentifierType> (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/EntityServiceBase.cs:279,309), ChildEntityServiceBase (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/ChildEntityServiceBase.cs:36,52,70), AuthUIService (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auth/AuthUIService.cs:214,227,273,288,315,426) and NotificationInboxService (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Notifications/NotificationInboxService.cs:46,64,84,101). Outside the framework it is called directly by services that sit outside the base hierarchy: Store's cart and lookup services (MMCA.Store/Source/Modules/Sales/MMCA.Store.Sales.UI/Services/ShoppingCarts/CartStateService.cs:93,140,174,206,260,297, MMCA.Store/Source/Modules/Sales/MMCA.Store.Sales.UI/Services/Lookups/CustomerLookupService.cs:27,73, MMCA.Store/Source/Modules/Sales/MMCA.Store.Sales.UI/Services/Lookups/ProductVariantLookupService.cs:29,94) and Helpdesk's single API client (MMCA.Helpdesk/Source/Hosts/UI/MMCA.Helpdesk.UI.Web/Services/HelpdeskApiClient.cs:30,50,64,84,95,109,122,138,149). Its own behavior is pinned by HttpResultExecutorTests, including the code literals (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/Api/HttpResultExecutorTests.cs:29-30), the timeout-versus-cancellation split (:150,164,178) and the rethrow paths (:192,206,219,230,240).
    • Caveats: a JsonException is classified as a transport fault, so a server that answers 200 with a body the client cannot deserialize produces the same generic "check the connection" message as a refused socket; the distinction is available in the error's Source but not in its code. The two user-facing messages are hard-coded English at the source; they reach a localized UI only when the page renders them through LocalizedErrorMessage, which replaces the sentence only while the error still carries the executor's own text (ResultUiExtensions.cs:364-371), so a page that displays Error.Message directly still shows English.

    PagedReadAll

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Api · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Api/PagedReadAll.cs:18 · Level 3 · class (static)

    • What it is: a helper that reads every row of an entity controller's /paged endpoint by requesting page after page until the server's reported total is reached, for hand-written services that need the whole set in one list (class summary, lines 8-11).
    • Depends on: Result and Result<T> for the return shape, PagedCollectionResult<T> and its PaginationMetadata for each page (imported through MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions and MMCA.Common.UI.Common, lines 3-4). Externals: BCL CultureInfo, string.Create, System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.
    • Concept introduced, a single read truncates silently. [Rubric §19, State Management & Data Flow] assesses whether the data a page holds is the data the server has. The remarks (lines 12-18) record the trap: the API clamps any requested page size to its own maximum (ApplicationSettings.MaxPageSize, 500 by default), and the GET-all endpoint ignores pageSize and always returns that maximum, so rows past it vanish with nothing to say so. Paging until PaginationMetadata.TotalItemCount is reached is the only unbounded route. [Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity] applies to the loop bound: a server that misreports its total cannot make the client spin forever.
    • Walkthrough
      • PageSize (line 22) is a public const int of 500, the API's default maximum, so no request is clamped (comment, line 21). MaxPages (line 28) is a private const of 40, the runaway guard of 20,000 rows (comment, lines 24-27).
      • LookupPageUrl(string entity, int pageNumber) (line 43) builds {entity}/paged?pageNumber=...&pageSize=500&sortColumn=Id&sortDirection=asc&includeFKs=false&includeChildren=false with string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...) (lines 44-46). Sorting by Id ascending keeps consecutive pages from skipping or repeating a row, and the doc comment (lines 30-38) makes the exact text part of a contract: a host that warms its output cache by replaying these URLs must replay them byte for byte. The CA1055 suppression (lines 39-42) keeps the return a string for that reason, since callers both compose it as text and wrap it as a relative Uri.
      • ReadAllAsync<T>(Func<int, Task<Result<PagedCollectionResult<T>>>> fetchPage, CancellationToken) (line 57) null-guards the delegate (line 61) and loops pageNumber from 1 to MaxPages (line 65). Each iteration checks cancellation first (line 67), fetches the page (line 69), and returns the first failure unchanged as Result.Failure<List<T>>(result.Errors) (lines 70-73). An empty page ends the loop (lines 75-79); otherwise the items are accumulated (line 81) and the loop ends once the count reaches TotalItemCount (lines 83-86). The method returns Result.Success(accumulated) (line 89), so hitting the 40-page guard yields the rows read so far rather than a failure.
    • Why it's built this way: the fetch is a delegate rather than an HttpClient, so each caller keeps its own transport choice (an authenticated SendRequestAsync, or an anonymous IdempotentReadRetry GET) and its own filters, while the paging rule lives once. Returning a Result rather than throwing keeps it inside the framework's client contract that a page branches on failures instead of catching them.
    • Where it's used: ADC UI services SpeakerLookupService (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Services/Speakers/SpeakerLookupService.cs:91), EventLookupService (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Services/Events/EventLookupService.cs:97), CategoryItemLookupService (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Services/Categories/CategoryItemLookupService.cs:37) and OrganizerFeedbackService (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Services/Feedback/OrganizerFeedbackService.cs:27,82). The ADC Conference service's SelfHttpOutputCacheWarmupTask replays URLs in the LookupPageUrl shape (MMCA.ADC/Source/Services/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/SelfHttpOutputCacheWarmupTask.cs:42). Pinned by PagedReadAllTests (MMCA.Common/Tests/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI.Tests/Services/Api/PagedReadAllTests.cs). OrganizerFeedbackService composes its own filtered /paged URLs with PagedReadAll.PageSize rather than LookupPageUrl (OrganizerFeedbackService.cs:32,87), since it needs an EventId or SessionId filter.

    IAuditHistoryUIService

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Auditing · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auditing/IAuditHistoryUIService.cs:11 · Level 3 · interface

    • What it is: the UI client contract for an audit-history endpoint (AuditHistoryControllerBase, ADR-075): one page of an entity's recorded changes, newest first (IAuditHistoryUIService.cs:6-10).
    • Depends on: Result<T> and AuditHistoryEntryDTO (IAuditHistoryUIService.cs:1-2).
    • Concept introduced: none new; it follows the same "no failure throws" client contract taught at ILegalAcceptanceUIService. The returns doc states the method never throws for a server answer (line 23).
    • Walkthrough: one member, GetPageAsync(routePrefix, entityAlias, entityKey, page, pageSize, cancellationToken) (line 24), reading {routePrefix}/{entityAlias}/{entityKey}?page={page}&pageSize={pageSize} (lines 13-16). The route prefix is the host's (for example Admin/Catalog/AuditHistory), the alias is the name the endpoint knows the entity by, and the key is the entity id as an invariant string (lines 17-19).

Its signature lines up with AuditHistoryPanel's FetchPage delegate once a page binds the first three arguments.

    ILegalAcceptanceUIService

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Legal · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Legal/ILegalAcceptanceUIService.cs:16 · Level 3 · interface

    • What it is: the UI-side contract for Terms of Service acceptance: read the signed-in user's standing, and record an acceptance of the version the user was shown. It is the dependency behind TermsAcceptanceGate (TermsAcceptanceGate.razor.cs:61).
    • Depends on: Result<T> (ILegalAcceptanceUIService.cs:1) and LegalAcceptanceDTO (MMCA.Common.Shared.Legal, ILegalAcceptanceUIService.cs:2); both calls target LegalAcceptanceRoutes.Path (ILegalAcceptanceUIService.cs:11).
    • Concept introduced, no failure should block the user. [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] assesses whether the client treats the API's error channel as a typed contract. The remarks say every member returns a Result carrying the API's own errors, including a 404 for a host that serves no such endpoint, and nothing throws for a server answer or a transport fault, so a caller can treat any failure as "do not block" (ILegalAcceptanceUIService.cs:10-15).
    • Walkthrough: GetAsync(cancellationToken) reads the standing via GET Users/me/legal-acceptance (:21). AcceptAsync(version, cancellationToken) records an acceptance via POST Users/me/legal-acceptance and returns the standing after acceptance (:27).
    • Why it's built this way: an interface keeps the gate component testable and lets a host swap the transport. The framework registers the default with TryAddScoped (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:211), so a consumer's own registration wins.
    • Where it's used: implemented by LegalAcceptanceUIService; consumed by TermsAcceptanceGate and by ADC's LegalAndDataCard (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.UI/Pages/Users/Profile/LegalAndDataCard.razor.cs).

    MMCA.Common.UI · MMCA.Common.UI.Services.Auditing · MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Auditing/AuditHistoryService.cs:21 · Level 4 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the default HTTP implementation of IAuditHistoryUIService, built on the shared authenticated client.

    • Walkthrough: GetPageAsync (line 27) rejects a null or blank route prefix, alias or key (lines 35-37), builds the relative URL with string.Create under the invariant culture, trimming a trailing slash from the prefix and escaping the alias and key with Uri.EscapeDataString (lines 39-41), then inside HttpResultExecutor.ExecuteAsync creates the authenticated client (line 46), sends the GET through RetryPolicy (lines 47-49) and reads the body as IReadOnlyList<AuditHistoryEntryDTO> (lines 51-52).
